However, this potential compensation never influences our analysis, opinions, or reviews. Our editorial content is created independently of our marketing partnerships, and our ratings are based solely on our established evaluation criteria. Read More
Cryptocurrency giant Binance faces what could be the largest exchange hack in history after a security breach affected an estimated $6.3 billion in digital assets, eclipsing the record-setting $1.5Bn Bybit exploit in 2025. The Binance hack has led the exchange to pledge to cover all losses, while investigators work to identify the attackers and recover the stolen funds.
Binance confirmed that the incident affected approximately $6.3Bn in digital assets, with around $3Bn reportedly frozen on-chain through coordination with blockchain partners and other platforms. However, a substantial portion of the funds may remain under the attackers’ control.
In a statement, Binance co-CEO Richard Teng reassured customers that their funds were safe and that the company would absorb the financial impact using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and corporate reserves. Former CEO CZ also spoke on the incident, saying on X, “User funds are safe..I don’t manage Binance anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”
The exchange also temporarily suspended withdrawals while undertaking a security overhaul of its withdrawal infrastructure and associated addresses. Deposits, however, remain unaffected and operational.
Compromised Engineer’s Laptop Suspected in the Binance Hack
Binance’s preliminary investigation indicates the attack may have originated from a DevOps engineer’s compromised laptop. This breach may have allowed attackers to access a service container, which they used to submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
However, Teng cautioned against viewing this incident as merely a case of stolen employee credentials. He noted that the attacker did not exploit just one engineer’s permissions or carry out a single action.
Instead, he described the incident as a more sophisticated, multi-stage attack. Binance has also emphasized that it has no evidence that any wallet private keys were exposed.
The exchange has revoked authorizations for affected addresses and engaged law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence specialists to trace transactions and recover assets.
Binance plans to publish a detailed technical post-mortem once it completes its investigation, along with an updated Proof of Reserves following the security remediation process.
North Korean Hackers Suspected, but Attribution Remains Unconfirmed
The identity of those responsible for the Binance hack remains uncertain, although two prominent cryptocurrency analytics firms have independently linked the incident to North Korean cybercriminals.
Both TRM Labs and Chainalysis have pointed to a North Korean hacking operation known as TraderTraitor. Chainalysis reportedly expressed high confidence in the group’s involvement, while TRM Labs identified similarities between the Binance incident and previous attacks attributed to North Korean-linked hackers.
On-chain sleuth ZachXBT also claims that TraderTraitor is responsible, linking wallet addresses from the Binance hack to those from the $388M Bitget exploit earlier this month.
Zach adds that after the Arbitrum Security Council froze $30M in stolen funds, the total amount frozen from the $6.3Bn hack sits at $2.83Bn. Tether, Circle, and Ripple account for most of it.
Binance has not confirmed these allegations and says it is working with law enforcement to identify the perpetrators. The suspected involvement of North Korean hackers is particularly significant given the country’s history of targeting cryptocurrency exchanges and digital asset platforms to generate funds.
The most recent major example was the February 2025 attack on Bybit, when hackers believed to be operating under the Lazarus Group stole about $1.5Bn in digital assets.
Within roughly two weeks, the attackers had converted at least $300M into unrecoverable funds. By August 2026, Bybit co-founder and CEO Ben Zhou said the exchange had recovered approximately $48.4M, with another $30.5M frozen.
Other Crypto Platforms Freeze Billions in Assets
As ZachXBT documented, the scale of the Binance incident has prompted action across the wider cryptocurrency industry. Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle have reportedly frozen about $2.83Bn in assets to prevent further movement of potentially compromised funds.
These interventions highlight the importance of centralized stablecoin issuers and blockchain analytics firms in responding to major cryptocurrency security incidents, particularly when stolen assets move across multiple networks and platforms.
Bitcoin also came under pressure following news of the breach, falling by more than 4% as markets reacted to the security concerns. It remains unclear whether the incident will have a lasting impact on investor confidence or broader cryptocurrency market sentiment.
Explore: The Best Token Presales
Binance Hack: What Does the Incident Mean for the World’s Largest Exchange?
Founded in 2017, Binance has grown into the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, serving hundreds of millions of registered users globally. Its platform offers spot trading, derivatives, digital wallets, savings products, and other financial services.
The company has faced significant regulatory scrutiny, including the 2023 resignation of founder Changpeng Zhao after he pleaded guilty to money laundering violations in the United States.
Despite the latest incident, Binance insists customer funds remain protected and has committed to absorbing the financial losses.
The immediate priority is to recover as much of the affected cryptocurrency as possible, identify those responsible, and ensure the exchange’s infrastructure is secure before resuming normal withdrawal services.
With the estimated impact potentially exceeding any previous cryptocurrency exchange hack, the incident tests Binance’s security systems, crisis management, and ability to maintain customer confidence.
Crypto Markets Holding Strong Amid the Biggest Exchange Hack in History: Bullish?
While this hack could be seen as a true black swan event for the markets, with over $6Bn in funds stolen from the world’s largest crypto exchange, the quick freeze of nearly $3Bn and Binance’s proactive response to the exploit, coupled with its leaders assuring investors that user funds are safe, the market is holding up incredibly well.
Bitcoin briefly fell to $76,500 as news of the Binance hack broke, but has already recovered to over $78,000, absorbing the sell-off with almost no effort. BNB, with its close ties to the exchange, has suffered more, dropping over -6% but is still holding above its longstanding $700 support zone.
Away from coins in the red, several tokens haven’t even flinched at the news and are up over the past 24 hours. Tron is one example: it is up +2% on the day, even though $234M worth of TRX was stolen in the hack.
Hyperliquid seems immune to bad news right now, continuing its recent rally with a +12% daily move as it climbed back above $90 earlier today and looks set to retest its $97 all-time high.
If the hack is brought under control and more funds remain frozen, expect Binance to reimburse users for any lost funds and absorb its own losses with little difficulty. If this happens, the worst is likely over for the crypto market, and it would highlight incredible strength heading into the year-end.

sources.news_title: Binance hack: ‘additional points of breach’ beyond a laptop
sources.text:
Binance now says a compromised laptop was not the only way in. Its investigation has “uncovered additional points of breach” in the attack that hit about $6.3bn of its assets on Thursday, the world’s largest crypto exchange said on Friday.
Binance said in an investigation update on X that it will cover all losses and has frozen about $3bn so far. Blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs puts the theft at $6.36bn in a report on the Binance hack. It calls it “the largest crypto theft on record” and attributes it to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state hacking unit. The previous record was the $1.5bn taken from rival exchange Bybit in February 2025.
“Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach,” Binance said.
Its first update, on Thursday night, said a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop may have let an attacker into a service container to submit unauthorised withdrawals. A later service update said the incident “stems from multiple factors”, with the compromised computer a possible entry point. A root-cause report will follow, Binance said.
Binance said it has found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. It will cover the losses from its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), an emergency reserve, and from company funds.
Twenty minutes on ten blockchains
The money started leaving Binance wallets at 20:05 UTC on 29 October, according to TRM. Most of it moved in about 20 minutes, across ten blockchains including Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana and the XRP Ledger. A second wave hit wallets on Avalanche and Polygon around 23:05 UTC.
Preparation began at least 36 hours earlier, TRM said. The attacker funded a wallet with small withdrawals from Tornado Cash, a service that hides where crypto comes from. It then rehearsed the attack on test wallets.
On Ethereum, the attacker used a feature called EIP-7702 to hand control of a Binance “hot wallet” to its own code. A hot wallet is one an exchange keeps online to pay out customer withdrawals. One transaction then moved 167,464 ETH and 63 other tokens, including 1.615 billion USDT, TRM said.
Wallets on the other chains sent funds through ordinary signed transfers in the same half hour. In TRM’s assessment, that points to an attacker who could make Binance’s signing system approve transactions on many chains. “Binance has yet to publish a root cause,” TRM wrote.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the attack was not a matter of one person’s access.
“To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer’s permissions, and this was not a single ‘one-click’ action,” Teng wrote on X.
He said the investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.
The freezes
Stablecoin issuers, which can block their own tokens, froze stolen funds within the hour. Tether froze 971.1 million USDT at 21:01 UTC, according to TRM. Circle froze 823 million USDC three minutes later. Ripple, World Liberty Financial and the Arbitrum network’s Security Council also froze funds.
TRM counted about $2.7bn frozen on-chain by 00:30 UTC on Friday. Binance’s figure is about $3bn. The attacker still holds more than 420,000 ETH and 18,270 BTC, about $2.4bn that no issuer can freeze, TRM said.
Before the freezes spread, the attacker sold about 325 million USDT for ETH at a discount of more than 10%, TRM said. It also borrowed ETH against USDT on the lending protocol Aave. Aave then froze the affected markets. The outflows stopped when Binance paused withdrawals, the exchange said.
Who is blamed, and who denies it
TRM said it makes its North Korea judgment “with high confidence”, based on on-chain and off-chain intelligence. The FBI named the same group as behind the Bybit theft, TRM noted. Chainalysis, another analytics firm, also tied the attack to the group and estimated $5.912bn stolen at the time of the theft.
Binance has not named a culprit. North Korea has denied involvement in hacks in the past, Osmond Chia reported for the BBC. In September, Bitget said it suspected North Korean hackers in the Bitget hack of its hot wallets. This month, the US charged 14 people over a scheme placing North Korean IT workers at more than 70 companies. The country’s hackers are also building their own AI tools.
What happens next
Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals on Thursday night. By Friday, it said deposits were operating normally. It is on track to resume withdrawals within 45 hours of its latest update, after a security revamp of its withdrawal service. Binance.US, a separate company, said it was not affected.
Bitcoin fell below $77,000 for the first time in more than a month on the news, Muyao Shen and Vildana Hajric reported for Bloomberg. Binance said it will publish a technical post-mortem and an updated proof of reserves once its investigation is complete.

sources.news_title: Binance hit by $6.3 billion hack in world's biggest crypto heist
sources.text:
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance said in a post on the social media platform X.
The exchange said customer funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 45 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, a $1 billion bitcoin reserve designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website.
Co-CEO Teng said that "and company funds" would cover losses.
The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.
TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation attributed to North Korea.
"TRM attributes the attack to... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible.
North Korea has for years used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to U.S. and South Korean authorities as well as cybersecurity experts.
North Korea routinely denies that.
"Your money is safe and we're covering every loss," Teng said on X. "Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual."
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly.
Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilized.
BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8%, while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended U.S. trading.
An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance's engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
"Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said. Later, the company added it had uncovered additional points of breach.
Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets.
"Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss," he said.
Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure due to higher U.S. interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.
World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.
The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
In September, Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.
"The broader credit and industry implications will depend on the ultimate losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence across the digital-asset ecosystem," said Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president, digital assets at Moody's Ratings.

sources.news_title: Blockchain intelligence firms link North Korea to $6.3B hack on Binanc
sources.text:
Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, said Friday that hackers stole more than $6 billion in what appears to be the largest cryptocurrency heist on record. Blockchain firms have pointed to the attack coming from a North Korean hacking unit.
The company said it has reserved more than $6.34 billion of company funds to cover the stolen assets and was beginning to recover assets for users. Binance worked with blockchain partners to freeze roughly $3 billion in affected assets.
The cryptocurrency exchange has promised to cover all losses, and it has been sharing regular updates on its social media channels as it uncovers more information about the hack.
“We are working nonstop to resolve this,” Binance’s co-CEO Richard Teng said Friday in a video posted to X.
In an exchange Friday with reporters at the White House, President Donald Trump said U.S. officials were investigating the Binance hack. Asked whether North Korea was involved, Trump said: “We’re looking at that.”
Here’s what we know about the hack, possible North Korean involvement and Binance’s investigation.
Binance said on X that an initial investigation suggested the incident may have involved a compromised laptop, but that a subsequent investigation uncovered additional “points of breach.”
U.S.-based blockchain intelligence firm TRM, in a post on its website late Thursday, attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as North Korea’s elite hacking unit. “We make this judgment with high confidence,” the firm said.
“An attacker moved approximately USD 6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes,” TRM said. “Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists.”
Blockchain analysis company Chainalysis also believed the Binance hack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor, its co-founder and CEO Jonathan Levin wrote on X.
Asked about the potential ties to North Korea, a Binance spokesperson said only that the company is “working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice.”
Experts say North Korea has turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties.
In December 2022, South Korea’s spy agency said North Korean hackers had stolen an estimated 1.5 trillion won ($1.1 billion) in cryptocurrency and other virtual assets in the past five years, more than half of it in 2022 alone. It said North Korea’s capacity to steal digital assets was considered among the best in the world.
While about half of the stolen assets were frozen, there is evidence that the hackers already are transferring and converting some of what wasn’t recovered, said Garrick Hileman, an independent cryptocurrency analyst.
“Like in money laundering, you bring in the stolen goods and launder those through a mixer or tumbler,” he said. “You mix it in with other cryptos, and it’s harder to track.”
How long it will take the hackers to turn that into something usable isn’t clear, he said. “The bottom line is there are places in the world where you can take your bitcoin and get that converted,” Hileman said.
TRM and several other crypto firms and experts have said the hack represents the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
In February of last year, another cryptocurrency exchange, Bybit, suffered a $1.5 billion hit when it was hacked. The FBI said North Korea and TraderTraitor were responsible for the hack. TRM listed the Bybit hack when it referenced similarities between the Binance hack and previous attacks linked to TraderTraitor.
Binance’s founder, Changpeng Zhao , wrote on X that while Binance’s hack might be the largest in terms of its dollar value, previous attacks on other companies like the crypto exchange Mt. Gox have had a more substantial impact in terms of the bitcoin amount affected, he said.
Experts warn this scale of hacking could become more commonplace.
“A cyber attack of this level is a matter of when, not if, particularly alongside the rise of AI,” said Andy Ward, a senior vice president at Absolute Security. “Cyber threats are becoming more sophisticated and widespread as ever, and it is likely only a matter of time before an even larger hack, with even greater financial fallout, makes headlines.”
The hack has raised questions about why stronger approval controls were not in place, said Kok Tin Gan, co-founder and CEO of cybersecurity firm NyxLab.
“This looks like one signature that gave the attacker a never-expiring, full-access token to a Binance hot wallet,” he said, referring to cryptocurrency wallets that hold users’ “private keys,” or unique authorizations, digitally and that are connected to the internet.
Teng, Binance’s co-CEO, confirmed in a nearly five-minute video posted on X Friday that Binance’s own hot wallet was affected. “User assets are held under Binance’s established security architecture,” he said. “The vast majority sits in cold wallets” — which are offline and used for secure storage — “and are only moved into a hot wallet when a user makes withdrawal.”
Teng said Binance’s tech and security teams are “still deep” in investigating the hack. He said it was not carried out by one person and that the attackers used complex tactics, including a “self-destruct mechanism” that is making the incident more difficult to investigate.
“We are working with law enforcement, blockchain intelligence firms, token issuers and other exchanges to trace and recover stolen funds,” Teng said. “We will do everything within our power to make sure that these bad actors will be held accountable.”
Binance has said deposits were unaffected, while withdrawals have been suspended and are expected to resume in the next day or two.
___
Associated Press writers John Seewer and Aamer Madhani contributed to this report.

sources.news_title: Crypto giant Binance hit by 'largest hack in history'
sources.text:
Crypto giant Binance hit by ‘largest hack in history’
The world’s largest cryptocurrency platform has been hit by one of the most severe hacks in history, affecting several billion dollars of digital assets and forcing it to freeze customer accounts.
Binance said on Thursday that some $6.3bn (£4.7bn) had been impacted by the attack, half of which has been frozen but still in its control. The other half remains in the hands of the hackers, according to the crypto giant, which promised to “cover all losses”.
The incident appeared to be triggered by an engineer’s laptop being compromised, granting the hacker access to the group’s systems to make withdrawals. Analysts have suggested the hack was carried out by a North Korean unit, though its involvement has not been confirmed.
A TRM Labs report pointed to several elements of the attack show similarities to a 2025 hack on the Bybit exchange – believed to be the next largest in history – which was carried out by North Korea’s Trader Traitor.
The research house’s head of policy Ari Redbord said the Binance hack was a “watershed moment” on a scale the industry had not seen.
Binance: User funds ‘completely safe’
Binance said its teams were “working around the clock” to resolve the issue”.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” it added in a statement.
The company, whose founder Changpeng Zhao pleaded guilty to money laundering before being pardoned by President Trump last year, has some 335m users registered globally. It is believed to have roughly $165bn assets under its control.
It added: “As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our security teams conduct checks, secure wallet infrastructure, and trace affected assets, with the close support of our law enforcement and industry partners.”
Major cryptocurrencies fell immediately through Asia’s trading session, with bitcoin shedding over three per cent to fall to a six-week low. Shares in Binance rival Coinbase also fell some 4.8 per cent and Strategy – a ‘crypto treasury’ that takes debt-fuelled bets on bitcoin – fell some six per cent in after hours US trading.
Zhao said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance”, adding that while he does not over see day-to-day management of the firm any more, “as a shareholder I expect all user funds will be fully covered.
“It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at Hashkey Group, based in Hong Kong.

sources.news_title: Here’s How Hackers Siphoned $300M in XRP from Binance in Latest Hack
sources.text:
On-chain data shows how hackers moved nearly $300 million worth of XRP from Binance during a major security breach that cost the exchange $6.3 billion.
On the evening of Oct. 29, blockchain monitoring platform Whale Alert flagged a large XRP outflow from Binance worth nearly $300 million. At first, the transaction looked like a regular exchange withdrawal and attracted little attention.
However, closer examination linked the transfer to what investigators now call one of the largest crypto exchange exploits in history, with a reported loss of about $6.3 billion.
Over 233M XRP Moved from Binance in 4 Minutes
The XRP transfers occurred within a four-minute window. At 8:05 PM UTC, the Binance (6) XRPL wallet activated a newly created address, rk2…zMx, by sending it 185 million XRP worth $235.8 million at the time.
Whale Alert recorded the transfer as a routine outflow, and the transaction data showed no sign of an ongoing breach. However, several more transfers followed within minutes, revealing a pattern of activity involving multiple Binance wallets.
At 8:07 PM UTC, the Binance (9) wallet sent 14.69 million XRP worth $18.7 million to the same address. Within another minute, the Binance (18) and Binance (15) wallets transferred 13.14 million XRP valued at more than $16.7 million and 11.955 million XRP worth $15.23 million, respectively, to rk2…zMx.
By 8:09 PM UTC, the Binance (10) wallet had sent another 8.655 million XRP worth more than $11 million to the address.
In total, five Binance wallets transferred 233.4 million XRP valued at $297 million to a single newly activated address in just four minutes. This pattern raised concerns within the XRP community.
XRPScan Flags the Address as Compromised
After receiving the transfers, the address rk2…zMx continued to hold the full 233.4 million XRP. At the time of reporting, the address had recorded no outgoing transactions since the final transfer arrived at 8:09 PM UTC.
XRPScan, a leading XRP Ledger block explorer, has since labeled the address as compromised, alerting the community that the account had been linked to a reported hack and that the assets sent to it likely represented stolen funds.
The XRP transfers marked the beginning of the broader Binance exchange hack, which reportedly resulted in losses exceeding $6 billion.
Compromised Laptop Linked to the Broader Attack
Binance’s initial investigation showed that the broader attack occurred due to a DevOps engineer’s compromised laptop. According to the exchange’s findings, the attackers used that access to enter a service container and carry out a series of unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
The exchange said its review found no evidence that attackers had obtained private keys from its wallets. This confirmed that the breach occurred at the application access level, not through a direct compromise of the cryptographic keys.
The attackers reportedly drained approximately $6.36 billion across ten different blockchains, completing most of the transactions within about 20 minutes.
Binance responded by suspending deposits and withdrawals while working with blockchain analytics firms and law enforcement agencies to trace the stolen funds and recover the assets.
These efforts allowed Binance’s partners to freeze approximately $3 billion on-chain. Tether contributed more than $1.56 billion in frozen stablecoin holdings to that total.
North Korean Hackers Identified as Suspects
Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis identified TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-sponsored hacking group, as the likely culprit behind the breach. Both firms highlighted similarities in the attack’s execution, the movement of assets, and the methods used to target the exchange.
Their findings also compared the Binance exploit to the February 2025 Bybit hack, which resulted in about $1.5 billion in losses. The FBI previously linked that attack to TraderTraitor.
Binance pledged to cover all losses suffered by users, using its approximately $1.2 billion Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) alongside additional company funds to cover any remaining shortfall. Co-founder Changpeng Zhao also publicly backed the commitment, stating that he expected every affected user to receive full compensation.

sources.news_title: Crypto giant loses £4,700,000,000 in 'largest heist in history'
sources.text:
The world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, says around $6.3billion (£4.7billion) worth of digital assets have been affected by ‘the largest hack in history’.
Binance has said roughly half of the assets had been frozen, but a significant amount remained in the hands of the suspected hackers.
The company has promised to ‘cover all losses’ caused by the incident, which it believes may have involved an engineer’s compromised laptop being used to make unauthorised withdrawals.
Two cryptocurrency analytics firms have linked the attack to a North Korean hacking group known as TraderTraitor.
TRM Labs said several details appeared similar to previous attacks allegedly carried out by North Korean hackers, including the record-breaking $1.5billion (£1.1billion) theft from crypto exchange Bybit in 2025.
Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs, described the Binance incident as a ‘watershed moment’ unlike anything the industry had seen before.
He warned that the attacker still appeared to control a huge amount of the affected assets, meaning efforts to track down and recover the money were far from over.
Another analytics firm, Chainalysis, said it had ‘high confidence’ that the North Korean group was linked to the incident.
Its head of research, Eric Jardine, urged other cryptocurrency exchanges to remain on alert, warning that platforms were attractive targets because of the enormous amounts of money they hold.
Binance has not directly confirmed whether North Korea was involved, but said it was working with law enforcement.
‘We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice,’ the company said.
Binance co-chief executive Yi He thanked cryptocurrency issuers for helping to freeze the affected funds.
She also confirmed that withdrawals had been temporarily suspended while the exchange checked that its systems were secure.
‘Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure,’ she said.
Jake Moore, who is Global Cybersecurity Advisor at ESET, told Metro: ‘It is worrying just how quickly billions of dollars can disappear in a modern-day cyber heist, but it is unbelievable that a single laptop has enough privileged access to enable it.
‘If a single device can authorise enormous cryptocurrency transfers, hackers can simply target systems and people until they find a weak link. And there is always one.
‘Consumers who choose to keep cryptocurrencies should spread their digital assets across multiple reputable platforms and secure hardware wallets (such as your own USB) to reduce the risk of losing everything in a single attack.’
Other major cryptocurrency companies have also taken action.
Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle said they had frozen around $2.4billion (£1.8billion) in assets linked to the potential hack.
Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800million (£600million) and was ‘closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance’.
World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, also said it had worked with partners to freeze stolen funds.
Concerns about a possible security breach at Binance had been raised by several people in the cryptocurrency industry hours before the company confirmed the incident.
Founded in China in 2017, Binance allows users to buy, sell and trade digital currencies and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
News of the incident has sent cryptocurrency prices tumbling, with Bitcoin falling by more than 4%. Ethereum and Solana also suffered sharp falls.

Millions in crypto at risk as Bitcoin price drops to six-week low after Binance hack

Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said Thursday it had “high confidence” that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing “robust on and off-chain intelligence.”

Experts say North Korea has turned to crypto hacking and other illicit cyber activities as a source of badly needed foreign currency to support its troubled economy and fund its nuclear program in the wake of tough U.N. sanctions and other difficulties.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, has suspended deposits and withdrawals following a suspected cyberattack estimated to have affected assets worth $6.3 billion.

According to Binance, preliminary findings suggest that the attack may have originated from a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer, which allegedly provided the attacker with access to a service container used to initiate unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
“Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions,” the company stated.
The exchange, however, said it had found no evidence that any wallet private keys were compromised, adding that a detailed technical report would be published after the investigation is concluded.
Binance disclosed that the estimated financial impact of the incident stood at approximately $6.3 billion, with about $3 billion worth of the affected assets already frozen on the blockchain through collaboration with its partners.
The company also assured users that they would not bear the financial consequences of the incident, promising to cover all losses through its Secure Asset Fund for Users, SAFU, and corporate funds.
“User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete,” Binance said.
As part of its immediate response, the exchange temporarily halted deposits and withdrawals while security checks were being conducted.
It also revoked the authorisation of the affected address and contacted law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and recover the assets.
Binance said its security and technical teams were working round the clock to resolve the incident, while collaborating with law enforcement agencies to identify and prosecute those responsible.
The company added that further details would be released as investigations progress.

sources.news_title: Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion From Binance in Biggest Crypto Heist Ever
sources.text:
Hackers Steal $6.3 Billion From Binance in Biggest Crypto Heist Ever
Hackers stole about $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts are calling the biggest crypto heist on record, Reuters reported Friday.
Binance halted withdrawals and promised to make customers whole. The Associated Press reported that deposits were paused as well, though the exchange told Reuters deposits were unaffected.
About $3 billion of the stolen assets has been located and frozen so far. The fate of the remaining $3.3 billion is unclear.
U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis both said they were highly confident North Korea was behind the attack. TRM pinned it on what it called North Korea’s elite hacking unit.
TRM said the attackers hit Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and moved most of the money in about 20 minutes, beginning late Thursday. The firm said the method mirrored the 2025 hack of exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to Pyongyang.
North Korea routinely denies using cyber units to steal money. Its diplomatic missions did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
A Hacked Laptop
Binance said an initial investigation suggests the breach may have started with a compromised laptop belonging to one of its engineers. That foothold let an attacker reach one of the exchange’s systems and make unauthorized withdrawals.
“Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” the company said.
“Your money is safe and we’re covering every loss,” co-CEO Richard Teng wrote on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” Binance expects to resume withdrawals within 48 hours.
Chainalysis’ Eric Jardine said the firm had confirmed at least $5.912 billion stolen as of 8:30 p.m. ET Thursday, according to a separate Reuters roundup.
Stablecoin issuer Tether froze nearly $1.57 billion linked to the theft, and Circle froze more than $800 million. Ripple froze about $200 million, and World Liberty Financial, the crypto firm tied to President Trump’s family, helped freeze about $29 million.
The news rattled crypto markets. Bitcoin fell to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether hit a two-month low of $2,178 before prices steadied, Reuters said. Shares of Coinbase, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8% in extended trading.
“It’s the biggest hack in history,” said Aravind Srinivasan of market maker GSR.
Tim Sun, a senior researcher at HashKey Group in Hong Kong, warned the breach “may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges.”
Binance has 335 million registered users and held about $162.8 billion in customer assets as of its 2025 annual report. Its emergency fund for users holds $1 billion in bitcoin, according to the exchange’s website.
The theft dwarfs the industry’s earlier losses. TRM Labs researchers counted $2.9 billion stolen across nearly 150 crypto attacks in all of last year, and exchange Bitget reported a roughly $350 million theft just last month.

sources.news_title: BREAKING: Lazarus Group suspected in $6.3 billion Binance hack
sources.text:
BREAKING: Lazarus Group suspected in $6.3 billion Binance hack
The Binance hack has been linked to North Korea’s Lazarus Group by blockchain investigators, who suspect the state-backed hackers stole approximately $6.3 billion from the cryptocurrency exchange on October 29.
- TRM Labs has linked the $6.3 billion Binance hack to North Korea’s TraderTraitor hacking unit with high confidence.
- Blockaid CEO Ido Ben-Natan said attackers moved at least $3.5 billion across four blockchains in under an hour.
- Investigators traced the theft to compromised transaction-signing controls, including 50 Ethereum authorizations targeting one hot wallet.
- Binance reported approximately $3 billion in frozen assets and pledged to cover customer losses.
- Withdrawals remain suspended during security upgrades, with Binance expecting services to resume within 48 hours.
According to TRM Labs, its investigators have attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, a North Korean hacking unit associated with Lazarus, with high confidence. Blockchain investigator ZachXBT separately identified Lazarus as the likely attacker, although Binance has not confirmed who carried out the theft.
In comments to crypto.news, Ido Ben-Natan, co-founder and CEO of blockchain security firm Blockaid, said the attack surpassed previous cryptocurrency thefts in scale.
“This is the biggest crypto hack in history. Our analysis shows at least $3.5 billion moved out of Binance hot wallets on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism and Avalanche in under an hour, more than double the Bybit theft in February 2025,” Ben-Natan said.
He noted that investigators had identified additional transfers involving Bitcoin and Tron, while his team continued tracing the stolen assets.
Meanwhile, blockchain tracking platform Onchain Lens reported that the Binance attacker had transferred 17,260 ETH, worth roughly $38.82 million, to a new wallet amid concerns that the funds could be laundered through Tornado Cash or other cryptocurrency mixers.
As per the tracker, the attacker still controlled almost 480,720 ETH, valued at $1.08 billion, which cannot be frozen by a token issuer. The receiving wallet was identified as 0x03b0eE5d82990cFF1bDa48651AC3e436d1a020ea.
Lazarus Group suspected as Binance hack reaches ten blockchains
TRM’s investigation traced about $6.36 billion leaving Binance-controlled wallets across ten blockchain networks, including Ethereum, Bitcoin, Tron, Solana and the XRP Ledger.
Most of the stolen funds were moved in a span of about 20 minutes, beginning at 20:05 UTC. Around $3.79 billion was transferred on Ethereum, while Bitcoin and Tron accounted for another $1.47 billion and $628 million, respectively.
Investigators identified 233.46 million XRP, worth nearly $296 million, leaving five Binance wallets before the Ethereum attack began.
The security firm said preparations started at least 36 hours before the theft. An attacker-controlled wallet received three small Tornado Cash withdrawals and tested malicious code before targeting Binance.
TRM linked the activity to TraderTraitor using blockchain transactions and other intelligence, although it did not publicly disclose all the evidence behind its attribution.
The FBI has previously identified that TraderTraitor was responsible for the February 2025 Bybit theft where approximately $1.5 billion was drained from the exchange. U.S. authorities have accused North Korean hacking operations of stealing cryptocurrency to help finance the country’s weapons programs.
Blockaid explains how attackers accessed Binance wallets
Blockaid’s technical investigation identified an unusual Ethereum transaction containing 50 EIP-7702 authorizations targeting Binance 14, one of the exchange’s busiest hot wallets.
EIP-7702 allows an Ethereum wallet to authorize smart contract code to operate on its behalf. The attacker prepared authorizations using 50 consecutive transaction counters, increasing the chance that one would match the wallet’s current counter.
Only one authorization succeeded, allowing a malicious contract to transfer assets from the wallet.
“The attacker effectively reprogrammed a major Binance Ethereum hot wallet so that a single operator could drain it, including any new money deposited into it,” Ben-Natan explained to crypto.news.
The attacker transferred approximately $2.5 billion from Binance 14, including 167,464 ETH and more than 1.6 billion USDT. Subsequent transfers targeted newly received funds.
Investigators found other Binance wallets moving assets through ordinary signed transactions across several networks. TRM believes the attacker may have gained access to the exchange’s transaction-signing infrastructure.
Binance identifies possible laptop compromise as $3 billion frozen
In its security update, Binance said its initial investigation pointed to a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop that may have allowed unauthorized access to an internal service container.
The exchange found no evidence of leaked private keys and said it would publish a detailed investigation once the cause was established.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino confirmed freezing more than 1.567 billion USDT, while Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire reported freezing over 800 million USDC. The Arbitrum Security Council secured approximately 74.6 million ARB and 8,425 ETH linked to the attacker.
Binance withdrawals remain paused
Binance has pledged to cover losses using its SAFU fund and company resources while working with law enforcement and blockchain investigators.
At the same time, the exchange said deposits remained operational, but withdrawals would stay paused while it upgraded withdrawal systems and address controls.
Binance expects withdrawals to resume within 48 hours and said a full report on the attack’s cause will follow.
Cryptocurrency markets also came under selling pressure following the hack, with Bitcoin briefly falling below $77,000. Total liquidations across the derivatives market exceeded $1.5 billion over 24 hours.

Hackers stole $6.3 billion ($8.9 billion) from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack ever, an attack that could prompt investors to rethink the risks of owning digital assets.
The hackers behind the raid were from North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. The attackers targeted Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and shifted most of the funds in about 20 minutes, TRM Labs said in a statement.
Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $US3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $US3.3 billion as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover “all hacking losses”.

Markets reacted immediately on Friday. Bitcoin dropped more than 3 per cent to a six-week low of $US76,368 and ether fell more than 3 per cent to a two-month low of $US2178.
TRM said several features of the attack matched earlier heists linked to North Korea, including a 2025 hack of crypto exchange Bybit that the US Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang.
“We make this judgment with high confidence,” it said in a statement.
The incident could be the world’s biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.
“It’s the biggest hack in history,” said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR’s systematic OTC business.
Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure lately due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
“It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $US162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report.
“User funds remain safe,” Binance said in a statement. “As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our security teams conduct checks, secure wallet infrastructure, and trace affected assets, with the close support of our law enforcement and industry partners.”
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website.
“It’s becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them,” said Bernardo Brites, chief executive of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.

The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $US2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $US350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.

$6.3B Binance Heist Could Be Biggest Crypto Heist Ever
sources.text:
$6.3B Binance Heist Could Be Biggest Crypto Heist Ever
|                                                       By                             Evann Gastaldo                                 withNewser.AI                                                                                   Posted Oct 30, 2026  12:30 AM CDT                                                       | 
Binance may have just set a record no one wants. Hackers are believed to have siphoned off $6.3 billion from the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange on Thursday, in what would be by far the biggest crypto theft to date, the Wall Street Journal reports. "It does look like a hack on Binance," founder Changpeng Zhao posted on X, while insisting "user funds are safe." Binance says it has temporarily halted deposits and withdrawals as it investigates, and says it will cover all losses, CNBC reports.
It was initially reported that Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle had frozen about $1.7 billion linked to the breach, but the total later announced would eclipse the $1.5 billion Bybit hack blamed on North Korea-linked actors in 2025, the largest crypto heist on record. That amount, however, has not yet been confirmed, the AP reports. About $3 billion is now reported to have been frozen. Binance's US platform says it was not impacted, and the company points to a $1.2 billion insurance fund to help absorb losses.

sources.news_title: Binance freezes assets after $6.3 billion heist, crypto industry's biggest
sources.text:
Binance freezes assets after $6.3 billion heist, crypto industry's biggest
- Binance said it worked with partners to freeze the affected assets with about $3 billion located so far
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange, in what analysts call the biggest crypto heist ever, attributed to North Korea, impacting market confidence.
- North Korea's alleged role in the record-breaking Binance hack.
- The $6.3 billion stolen, marking the largest crypto heist ever.
- Immediate market impact on Bitcoin, Ether, and other cryptocurrencies.
- Binance's response, asset freezing, and commitment to cover losses.
SINGAPORE/HONG KONG: Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack ever, an attack that could prompt investors to rethink the risks of owning digital assets.
The hackers behind the raid were from North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.
The attackers targeted Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and shifted most of the funds in about 20 minutes, TRM Labs said in a statement.
Binance said it worked with partners to freeze the affected assets with about $3 billion located so far.
It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion, and its co-founder Yi He said the exchange would cover “all hacking losses”.
Binance said its deposits were unaffected and it expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours.
TRM said several features of the attack matched earlier heists linked to North Korea, including a 2025 hack of crypto exchange Bybit that the US Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang.
“We make this judgment with high confidence,” it said in a statement.
North Korea’s mission in Geneva and its embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
The incident could be the world’s biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.
“It’s the biggest hack in history,” said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR’s systematic OTC business.
Markets reacted immediately in Asian trading on Friday.
Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178.
BNB , a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.
Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading.
Hacked laptop
An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
“The incident stems from multiple factors. Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” Binance said.
Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
Binance set to lose EU licence bid, permission to offer services in the bloc, sources say
“It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report.
“User funds remain safe,” Binance said in a statement.
Binance has secure asset fund
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website.
“It’s becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them,” said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.
“My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn’t cover a hack of meaningful size.”
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance’s Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.
Incident adds to string of crypto thefts
Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor.
The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers.
Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.
Binance, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.
Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.
In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider.
It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

sources.news_title: The $6.3 billion Binance hack: What we know so far about the biggest crypto heist in history
sources.text:
The crypto world is reeling after a hacker drained billions of dollars from Binance, the world’s largest digital currency exchange, on Thursday. The full details of the hack are still emerging, but the broad strokes of what happened are becoming clearer, as everyone from security researchers to Elon Musk to the company itself weigh in on the incident, which was almost certainly carried out by North Korea. (This story was updated on October 30 at 4:30pm ET with additional information).
Binance posted on X late Thursday evening Eastern Time, stating that a compromised developer laptop is partly to blame for the catastrophe, which is by far the biggest security incident in an industry that has been plagued by hacking since its earliest days. The company plans to provide more extensive details, and in the meantime, many other big crypto firms—including its biggest rivals—have rushed in to aid Binance. Here is a detailed look at what we know so far about the nature and scope of the hack, and what is likely to happen next.
How did Binance get hacked?
Reports of a hack began surfacing on X early on Thursday afternoon. That’s when crypto observers, referring to public blockchain data, pointed to large amounts of currency moving out of wallets associated with Binance. Soon after, company cofounder Changpeng Zhao confirmed the hack.
In its post on Thursday evening, Binance stated the hacker appeared to have gained control of a laptop belonging to an employee or a contractor. The company wrote that the “initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.”
Since that posting, crypto and security researchers have noted that the hackers essentially hijacked internal Binance wallets in order to “sweep” the funds to external wallets they controlled. They did this by using features of the Ethereum protocol that also let them help cover their tracks and lock out Binance security teams.
Mid-day Friday, Binance co-CEO Richard Teng provided an additional update saying the attack was more pervasive than one laptop. He wrote: “This was not carried out by one person. Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach.
This was a complex attack. The attacker also used a self-destruct mechanism that destroyed tooling and traces as they went, making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate.”
How much did the hacker steal?
Reports on X have suggested the hacker made off with anywhere from $2 billion to $8 billion, but in its post, Binance said the estimated total impact sits at around $6.3 billion. The situation is still fluid, and it could be days before the scope of the hack is finally determined.
What currencies did the hacker steal?
Early reports say the hacker took $1.5 billion in Bitcoin and around the same amount in the stablecoin Tether, and slightly under a billion dollars worth of Ethereum and the USDC stablecoin. It is likely the hacker stole various other currencies, too.
Who is behind the hack?
No one has claimed responsibility for the hack, and Binance has not pointed to a specific culprit, but security firms TRM and Chainalysis have both said North Korea is almost certainly behind it.
This theory is highly plausible given that the North Korean military has long used crypto hacking to help fund its operations. The sophisticated nature of the hack, which included efforts to move the funds after they were stolen, is also consistent with the tactics of North Korea. For now, though, there is no definitive proof the country is responsible.
Are the funds gone for good?
Soon after news of the hack became public, Tether and Circle—the firms responsible for minting USDT and USDC, respectively—announced they would freeze any stablecoins tied to the hack.
While this is ostensibly good news, other reports indicate these efforts may only be partially successful at best. That’s because there is evidence the hacker immediately took the stolen funds to the online crypto lending platform Aave, and posted them as collateral for a loan in Ethereum. This means the hacker is now in a position to walk off with the borrowed Ethereum. Since news of the Aave stunt was reported, others have reported that the loan only amounted to around $60 million so the vast bulk of the stablecoins should be recovered.
What has been the impact on crypto markets?
Unsurprisingly, the price of all major cryptocurrencies fell upon news of the hack, though the drop was not dramatic. Bitcoin and Ethereum are down around 3% as of early Friday, but that drop also coincided with a selloff in the broader financial markets.
The relatively muted reaction suggests the market is confident that Binance has deep enough pockets to absorb the loss while also keeping its customers whole.
What have been the reactions to the hack?
In the immediate wake of the hack, the CEOs of Coinbase, Tether, and other big crypto companies all pledged to support Binance in its hour of need. In response, Binance’s cofounder noted that “many industry friends and even competitors (including some previously-not-so-friendly ones) provided very much needed help.” Meanwhile, on Friday, new reports said Binance is working with the FBI and the U.S. Secret Service to investigate the hack.
Zhao also expressed thanks to Yi He, the company’s current co-CEO, for pulling an all-nighter while she is pregnant.
Meanwhile, some on X expressed incredulity that Binance’s security could be so flawed as to allow a hacker to steal billions simply by gaining access to a single company laptop. As for Elon Musk, he chimed in with an AI-focused take, saying, “Super intelligence agents will at some point do this to gain currency for themselves, not a human.”

sources.news_title: Binance hit by record $6.3bn crypto hack blamed on North Korea
sources.text:
Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies tumble as the exchange races to freeze stolen assets and reassure investors
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Stablecoin issuers including El Salvador-based Tether and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial froze about half of the stolen assets.
Binance is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the United States Secret Service (USSS), a person familiar with the situation told Reuters.
“This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance said in a post on X.
The exchange said customer funds were safe and it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It said earlier on Friday it expected to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.
Binance said the company had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses, without giving details about where the funds had come from. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.
The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.
TRM said the attackers were able to order Binance wallets to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korea.
“TRM attributes the attack to … North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” the firm said in an analysis posted on its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible.
British blockchain analysts Elliptic also said they believed North Korea was behind the theft.
“This incident is almost certainly the single largest known theft of any kind,” Elliptic said.
‘BIGGEST HACK IN HISTORY’
North Korea has for years used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to US and South Korean authorities as well as cybersecurity experts.
North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
The US embassy in London said it had no comment on a possible investigation. The USSS did not respond to a request for comment sent via email outside of US hours.
Abu Dhabi’s Financial Services Regulatory Authority, which issued Binance’s main operating licence, said it was “engaging closely with Binance and monitoring the incident”.
“Your money is safe and we’re covering every loss,” Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.”
“It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said, as crypto prices fell broadly.
Bitcoin BTC= hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether ETH= fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised.
BNB BNB=CCCL, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5.3% over the past 24 hours at $699.54, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares.
COMPROMISED LAPTOP
An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
“Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” Binance said. The company later added it had uncovered additional points of breach.
Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
“It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group.
HACK SIZE TOPS BINANCE SECURE ASSET FUND
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.
World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said.
The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
In September, Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform.
“The broader credit and industry implications will depend on the ultimate losses, affected counterparties, asset recovery, and importantly, whether the incident leads to wider disruption or loss of confidence across the digital-asset ecosystem,” said Cristiano Ventricelli, vice president, digital assets at Moody’s Ratings.
Where Binance’s $6.3 billion breach ranks in crypto’s biggest hacks and heists
| Time period | Company | What was stolen | What happened | 
| February 2025 | Cryptocurrency exchange Bybit | Digital tokens worth $1.5 billion | The crypto was taken from a “cold wallet” – a digital wallet usually stored offline and so supposedly more secure – that was used for ether tokens. | 
| March 2022 | Ronin Network, a network that allows transfer of crypto coins across different blockchains | Roughly $540 million from a blockchain project linked to the popular online game Axie Infinity | Hackers stole some 173,600 ether tokens and 25.5 million USD Coin tokens. | 
| February 2022 | Wormhole, a DeFi site | $320 million | Hackers making off with 120,000 digital tokens connected to the second-largest cryptocurrency, ether. The crypto arm of Chicago-based Jump Trading, which had the year before acquired the developer behind Wormhole, later replaced the funds. | 
| August 2021 | Poly Network, a platform that facilitates peer-to-peer token transactions | $610 million (Hackers behind the heist later returned nearly all of the stolen funds) | The hack underscored vulnerabilities in the burgeoning decentralised finance, or DeFi, sector, where users lend, borrow and save in digital tokens, bypassing the traditional gatekeepers of finance such as banks and exchanges. | 
| January 2018 | Tokyo-based exchange Coincheck | $530 million | The thieves attacked one of Coincheck’s “hot wallet” – a digital folder stored online – to drain the funds, drawing attention to security at exchanges.South Korea’s intelligence agency said at the time that a North Korean hacking group may have been behind the heist. | 
| Between 2011 and 2014 | Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox | Bitcoin worth close to $500 million was stolen in one of the earliest and most high-profile crypto hacks. | Mt. Gox, which once handled 80% of the world’s bitcoin trade, filed for bankruptcy in early 2014 after the hack was revealed, with some 24,000 customers losing access to their funds. |

sources.news_title: Crypto giant Binance says $6.3bn assets stolen in 'largest hack in history'
sources.text:
Crypto giant Binance says $6.3bn assets stolen in 'largest hack in history'
NEW YORK — Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that about $6.3 billion of digital assets were stolen in a “security incident” that has been described as the largest crypto heist in history.
The world’s largest crypto exchange said it had suspended all deposits and withdrawals and that about $3 billion in funds had been frozen with the help of other platforms following the apparent hack.
Binance said an initial investigation suggested that a hacker had been able to make unauthorized transactions after gaining access to an engineer’s compromised laptop.
The company said it would cover all losses, adding that user funds were “safe”.
“Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly,” Binance said in a statement.
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs has attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5 billion hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
"We make this judgment with high confidence," TRM said in a report, adding that several elements of the attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
The lab's chief policy officer Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.
Binance did not directly respond to queries about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
The incident concerns Binance.com, while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for US residents, said its platform is not affected by the issue.
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
"Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said.
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they have frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.
Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his firm is "closely tracking reports of a potential exploit involving Binance" and that his company has frozen more than $800m in assets linked to the incident.
Circle is the issuer and co-creator of the USDC, one of the world's largest US dollar-backed cryptocurrencies.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said his firm has frozen around $1.6bn "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."
"Protecting the industry and our partners is our main priority," said Ardoino, whose company issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.

sources.news_title: Binance hit by major hack as billions in crypto funds are frozen
sources.text:
Cryptocurrency platform Binance said on Thursday it had fallen victim to a major hack that hit around $6.3 billion (€5.5bn) in funds, with about half that amount frozen to prevent a massive theft.
The company - the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes - posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages on X, insisting that "user funds are completely safe" but also saying it would "cover all losses".
Binance later said on its X account for Latin America that "the total estimated impact is around $6.3bn (€5.5bn)".
"We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze the affected assets, with ~ $3bn (€2.6bn) frozen on-chain so far," it added.
That would be more than four times the amount involved in what had been the biggest-ever cyberattack of its kind to date: $1.5bn (€1.3bn) taken in February 2025 from the Bybit platform.
The Bybit heist was attributed at the time to a group of hackers affiliated with North Korea called TraderTraitor.
Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said on Thursday it had "high confidence" that the Binance hack was also orchestrated by TraderTraitor, citing "robust on and off-chain intelligence".
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists," TRM said.
TraderTraitor is believed to be part of Lazarus Group - which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for "The Interview", a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
Fund freeze
At about 0030 GMT (0230 CEST) on Friday, Binance said all deposits and withdrawals had been "temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement".
"This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets," the company said.
The company's statement on X said an initial investigation suggested the hack involved a compromised laptop belonging to a "DevOps engineer", allowing the unauthorised party to access a "service container" and execute unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
"We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets," Binance said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete.
Paolo Ardoino, the boss of Tether - a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT - said his firm had frozen about $1.6bn (€1.4bn) "related to a potential Binance exchange hack".
Jeremy Allaire, who runs cryptocurrency platform Circle, said his company had frozen more than $800m (€696m) in USDC.
USDT and USDC are both "stablecoins", or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar.
The US Department of Justice and the FBI did not immediately respond to requests for comment.
Crypto prices tumble
For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.
The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack, with the exception of stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins.
At about 0400 GMT (0600 CEST), bitcoin and Ethereum were down 0.8%, recovering after plunges of nearly 5% and nearly 6%, respectively. BNB, Binance's native cryptocurrency, was up 2.7% after tumbling nearly 10%.
The attack on Binance comes as many observers express concerns that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.
