Binance Halts Withdrawals After Suspected Hack as Tether, Circle Freeze $2.38B
sources.text:
Binance Halts Withdrawals After Suspected Hack as Tether, Circle Freeze More Than $2.38B
Binance is investigating a suspected security breach with an estimated $6.3 billion impact
Binance has temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while investigating a security incident that it estimates had a total impact of around $6.3 billion (£4.70 billion). The cryptocurrency exchange said its preliminary findings suggest a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle have frozen more than $2.38 billion (£1.78 billion) in assets linked to the incident. Binance said around $3 billion (£2.24 billion) had been frozen on-chain through work with blockchain partners, although the figures do not establish how much cryptocurrency was stolen.
The exchange said it had found no evidence of a wallet private key leak and pledged to cover all losses using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company funds. It said the investigation was continuing.
Binance Outlines Possible Cause of Incident
In an update posted on X, Binance said its initial investigation suggested a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer may have allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
The exchange stressed that the findings remained preliminary. It did not identify the suspected attacker or confirm the full extent of any losses.
Binance said it had revoked the affected address authorisation and was working with law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover assets. Deposits and withdrawals were suspended as a precaution while security checks continued.
The exchange said it would publish a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation was complete and the facts had been verified. It also plans to publish an updated proof of reserves after remedial work has finished.
Tether and Circle Freeze Billions
Circle chief executive Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million (£597.42 million)in USDC associated with the incident, in coordination with law enforcement. Tether chief executive Paolo Ardoino separately said his company had frozen nearly $1.57 billion (£1.17 billion) in USDT linked to the suspected attack.
Together, the freezes announced by the two stablecoin issuers exceed $2.38 billion (£1.78 billion). Binance's reported on-chain total of around $3 billion includes assets frozen through cooperation with other blockchain partners.
Binance's estimated $6.3 billion impact figure should not be interpreted as a confirmed theft. The exchange has not disclosed a final loss total, and the investigation is ongoing.
Binance Pledges To Cover Losses
Binance said it would cover all losses arising from the incident using its SAFU fund and company funds. The exchange described the fund as part of its response to protecting users during the incident and said customer funds were safe.
It also said it was working with law enforcement partners to establish the identity of those responsible and recover affected assets. Binance urged customers to rely on official channels for updates and contact customer support with questions.
Bitcoin Falls as Security Concerns Grow
Bitcoin fell 3.2 per cent to below $79,000 (£58,900) on Thursday, according to the Associated Press. The incident has renewed concerns about cryptocurrency exchange security, particularly hot wallets, which remain connected to the internet to facilitate digital asset transfers.
In February 2025, hackers stole approximately $1.5 billion (£1.12 billion) in cryptocurrency from exchange Bybit, one of the largest confirmed cryptocurrency thefts on record.
Binance has yet to publish its full technical findings. The cause of the incident, the final value of any losses and the amount of assets that can be recovered remain subject to the ongoing investigation.

Hackers steal $6.3 bil. from Binance in record heist blamed on North Korea
Summary
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance in a breach that analysts blamed on North Korea, prompting the exchange to halt withdrawals and say it would cover the losses. Binance said customer funds were safe and that it had located about $3 billion of the stolen assets with partners. The attack unfolded mostly within about 20 minutes late Thursday, and cryptocurrency prices fell before markets stabilized. Binance said it expected to resume withdrawals within 48 hours.
Key Facts
- Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the losses, and its website describes a separate $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund for protecting customer assets during security breaches.
- Tether said it froze nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.
- Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the attack involved a compromised laptop and malicious software designed to erase traces, and that hackers manipulated a transaction-approval system to move funds from an internet-connected wallet.
- Bitcoin fell to a six-week low of $76,368, ether dropped more than 3 percent to a two-month low of $2,178, and BNB was down 6.2 percent over 24 hours at $702.

SINGAPORE/HONG KONG — Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a theft that analysts blamed on North Korea and said could be the largest financial heist of all time.
Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would use company funds to cover the losses. Stablecoin issuers including El Salvador-based Tether and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial froze about half of the stolen assets.
The exchange said customer funds were safe and it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It said earlier on Friday it expected to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.
Binance said it had set aside around $6.34 billion of company funds internally to cover the losses. The company has a $1 billion bitcoin reserve fund designed to protect customer assets in the event of security breaches, according to its website. Binance founder Changpeng Zhao said on X that the company owned SpaceX shares worth more than $1 billion.
"We NEVER use any customer funds, so they are not impacted," Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said in a post on X.
Teng described the breach as a "complex attack" that was not carried out by one person and included a compromised laptop as well as malicious software designed to delete traces and evidence of its activity as it went along, "making it more difficult for us to trace and investigate."
The hackers were able to manipulate a system used to approve transactions to move money out of a Binance-controlled, internet-connected wallet in a way that did not pass through normal approval controls, Teng said.
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.
'Biggest hack in history'
The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
The bulk of the Binance heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.
TRM said the attackers were able to order Binance wallets to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the FBI attributed to North Korea.
"TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea's elite hacking unit," the firm said in an analysis on its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible.
"This incident is almost certainly the single largest known theft of any kind," British blockchain analysts Elliptic said.
North Korea has for years used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to U.S. and South Korean authorities as well as cybersecurity experts.
North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not respond to requests for comment.
Binance is working with the Federal Bureau of Investigation and the United States Secret Service (USSS), a person familiar with the situation told Reuters.
The FBI said it was "aware of the incident and is engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity, evaluate potential impacts, and coordinate appropriate investigative steps."
The USSS did not respond to an emailed request for comment.
Abu Dhabi's Financial Services Regulatory Authority, which issued Binance's main operating licence, said it was "engaging closely with Binance and monitoring the incident".
"It's the biggest hack in history," Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said, as crypto prices fell broadly.
Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3 percent to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilised.
BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 6.2 percent over the past 24 hours at $702, according to CoinMarketCap, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares.
Security implications
Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for the crypto sector, which had already been under pressure due to higher U.S. interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group.
Investor Michael Saylor, among Bitcoin's most prominent supporters, said in a post on X that he expected Binance to "deliver" on ensuring no customers suffered losses. "Our industry will learn from this incident, strengthen security, and emerge stronger and more resilient," he wrote on Friday.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of its 2025 annual report.
Abu Dhabi-backed investment group MGX became a minority investor in Binance last year. MGX declined to comment.

'Biggest hack in history': Crypto exchange Binance freezes assets after $6.3 b. security breach
sources.text:
North Korean hackers were behind a $6.3 billion raid on cryptocurrency exchange Binance, according to US blockchain analysis firm TRM Labs.
"An attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes," TRM Labs said in a blog post on its website.
"TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea's elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence. We make this judgment with high confidence."
Earlier in the day, Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said a security breach had resulted in an estimated $6.3 billion impact that analysts said could amount to the biggest crypto heist ever and might make investors rethink the risks of owning digital assets.
Binance said it had worked with partners to freeze the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It gave no update on the status of the remaining $3.3 billion as Binance co-founder Yi He said the company would cover "all hacking losses."
An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said.
Markets reacted immediately in early Asian trading on Friday.
Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368 and ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.
Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading.
The incident could be the world's biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.
"It's the biggest hack in history," said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR's systematic OTC business.
Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure lately due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange's 2025 annual report.
"User funds remain safe," Binance said in a statement. "As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our security teams conduct checks, secure wallet infrastructure, and trace affected assets, with the close support of our law enforcement and industry partners."
Binance has secure asset fund
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, according to its website, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches.
"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them, said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.
"My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said on Thursday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Binance's Yi said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.
Incident adds to string of crypto thefts
Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor, though the exact cause had not been confirmed. Morel said the incident began around 4:30 p.m. EDT and appeared to be ongoing.
The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.
Authorities have warned that organized crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.
Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.
Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.
In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

sources.news_title: World’s largest crypto exchange hit by suspected North Korean hack in world’s largest heist
sources.text:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, suspended withdrawals after hackers broke into its digital wallets and stole $6 billion in what appears to be the biggest crypto heist ever.
Binance said late Thursday that its initial investigation indicated the hack went through an engineer's laptop, "which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions." Blockchain evidence suggests the hack originated in North Korea, according to multiple crypto-tracing firms.
A team of cryptocurrency firms managed to freeze about $3 billion of the stolen loot amid a frenetic battle with the hackers to find and control the digital money.
Binance co-CEO Richard Tend said on X that the attack was not a "one-click" action, but rather a complex process. The investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual nor found evidence of any wallet private key leak.
Binance said it would cover all losses from the company's funds and an emergency assets fund, adding "user funds are safe." The crypto exchange said it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals to allow security checks to be completed and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds. The crypto exchange expects withdrawal services to resume by Sunday morning.
Crypto-tracing firm TRM Labs attributed the heist to an elite North Korean hacking unit "based on robust on and off-chain intelligence," pointing out that "several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists."
Pangolin Intelligence, another blockchain-tracking firm based in Singapore, said it also believed that a North Korean hacking unit was behind the heist.
"Analyzing the on-chain activity related to this hack and correlating with information gathered from previous known incidents" led to the attribution, said an analyst with Pangolin Intelligence, who did not want to be named for privacy reasons.
"I think the cat and mouse game has barely begun yet," the Pangolin Intelligence analyst told CNN, adding that North Korea was likely poised to tap a network of money laundering organizations to try to cash out the stolen funds.
Chainalysis, another crypto-tracking company, said it was monitoring stolen funds "moving across multiple blockchains," including bitcoin and ethereum. A Chainalysis spokesperson told CNN the firm had "high confidence" North Korea was behind the hack.
CNN has reached out to North Korea's mission at the UN for comment. Pyongyang has previously denied hacking allegations.
CNN has requested comment from the FBI, as well as the US Secret Service, which also investigates cybercrime. In past investigations of big crypto hacks, the FBI has had an on-call team of analysts that worked to freeze some of the money.
If North Korea is proven to be the culprit, it would be little surprise to US law enforcement officials and private experts. North Korean hackers were blamed for the previous record-high crypto hack, when they allegedly stole $1.5 billion from Bybit, another major cryptocurrency exchange. In that case, the attackers stole an amount equal to a significant portion of North Korea's reported annual gross domestic product in a matter of minutes.
North Korea's formidable hacking teams are a key source of revenue for the nuclear-armed, sanctions-battered regime, according to current and former US and South Korean officials. Pyongyang-linked hackers have stolen billions of dollars from banks and cryptocurrency firms in the last several years, according to reports from the United Nations and private firms.
A 2023 CNN investigation spotlighted how the South Korean intelligence service worked with private crypto-tracking experts to seize about $1 million in cryptocurrency that North Koreans had stolen from a victim.
Unlike platforms for trading stocks, cryptocurrency exchanges tend to hold digital assets on their users' behalf, which make them more vulnerable to hackers and theft, particularly given a lack of regulatory oversight within the relatively nascent industry.
Binance was co-founded in 2017 by Canadian national Changpeng Zhao, becoming the world's largest crypto trading platform within a year of its launch.
However, Zhao stepped down in 2023 after pleading guilty to violating anti-money laundering laws in the US. He was sentenced to four months in federal prison, and was pardoned by President Donald Trump in October last year.
Zhao, who no longer manages the platform but remains its largest shareholder, said on X that he expects user funds to be fully covered by the exchange, pushing back against any suggestion to the contrary in a spat on X with Elon Musk.
Prices of bitcoin and ether, the most widely traded cryptocurrencies, plummeted following news of the Binance breach, but regained some losses to trade about 2-3% lower midday Friday in Hong Kong.

sources.news_title: Billions of dollars stolen in largest cryptocurrency hack in history
sources.text:
Billions stolen as Binance targeted in largest cryptocurrency hack in history
In short:
Crypto watchers are reporting up to $US6.3 billion ($8.9 billion) in digital funds were stolen this morning, with more than $US3 billion currently frozen.
It appears the funds were moved after attackers compromised a staff member's laptop.
What's next?
Binance has moved to reassure users their funds are completely safe and it will cover all hacking losses.
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has suffered the largest hack in the sector's history, with attackers attempting to steal $US6.3 billion ($8.9 billion) in digital funds this morning.
The true scale of the theft is still unclear, with approximately $US3 billion ($4.2 billion) in funds currently frozen.
"This is definitely the largest [crypto hack] to date," said Nicholas Turnbull, a blockchain forensics expert and the director of Crypto Consulting Australia.
"You won't know [the full impact] until the dust all settles down."
Binance confirmed in a statement to ABC News that it had been the victim of an attack, saying hackers may have gained access to a staff member's laptop.
"We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak," a company spokesperson said in a written statement.
Binance also said users should "rest assured that … [their] funds are completely safe".
It added that the company, which is the world's largest crypto exchange, would cover all losses.
It appears the funds were moved from a number of "hot wallets" — internet connected wallets designed for high-speed everyday trading.
Thirty or 40 different tokens were affected, including Etherium, Bitcoin, and stablecoins such as USDT and USDC, according to crypto watchers.
RMIT economics professor Chris Berg, who specialises in blockchain technology, said not all the funds that attackers tried to steal will necessarily be successfully stolen.
"There are different layers of defence," he said. "Stablecoin providers can freeze those funds.
"[The hackers] have to withdraw it through an exchange somehow and that represents its own difficulty."
Binance said it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals "while security checks are completed", and that an investigation was underway.
"We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice," it said.
Binance later announced it had begun "recovering affected assets for users" and was working with law enforcement, issues and blockchain intelligence firms to "trace, freeze and recover additional funds".
"Binance has already reserved over $6.34B of company funds to cover this incident," it said.
"$5B of these funds are already held in the exact token assets that were impacted."
While the precise losses were not yet known, it was clear the Binance hack was significantly larger than the next largest crypto theft on record, in February 2025, when the North Korean-linked Lazarus group stole approximately $US1.5 billion from another cryptocurrency exchange, ByBit.
Mr Turnbull said Lazarus Group was a likely focus for investigation in the Binance case too.
"This was a pretty sophisticated attack … you've got multiple angles coming on … so it's definitely a group," he said.
Professor Berg said the cryptocurrency sector has been plagued by cybersecurity incidents.
"It's one of the themes of the industry," he said.
There are concerns that improvements in hacker capabilities driven by AI, amplify that risk.
"[The Binance hack] may well be connected to what's been going on … around AI," Professor Berg said.
"For the last month or so, we've had a series of hacking incidents and discoveries of cybersecurity vulnerabilities … driven by frontier AI models.
"The hackers will definitely be using AI because everybody is using AI.
"The question is, was this only possible because of advances in AI?"

sources.news_title: Binance halts withdrawals as suspected hack spurs crypto sell-off, vows to ‘cover all losses’
sources.text:
Binance estimates US$6.3 billion hacked in crypto’s biggest heist
Blockchain intelligence firms all point to North Korea as behind the breach
[NEW YORK] Crypto exchange Binance has suffered a US$6.3 billion hack, the largest to hit the digital-asset industry and the latest in a slew of security incidents afflicting the financial sector.
The world’s largest crypto trading platform suspended all withdrawals on Friday (Oct 30) and pledged to cover all losses. Binance said in a post on X that about US$3 billion of the assets had been frozen on blockchain networks. In another post, co-founder Yi He said that withdrawals were expected to resume by Sunday.
While the full details of the Binance breach have yet to emerge, the incident comes amid growing concern about the risks posed by hackers in the age of artificial intelligence.
Other recent cyberattacks have hit prediction market Polymarket, South Korean financial firms Mirae Asset Global Investments and Daishin Securities, as well as Japanese currency trading platform GMO Internet Group.
Blockchain intelligence firms TRM Labs, Chainalysis and Elliptic have all pointed to North Korea as behind the Binance heist. TRM called it “the largest crypto theft on record”. The funds drained in the attack were a mix of the largest cryptocurrencies, including Bitcoin, Ether, and the dollar-backed stablecoins USDT and USDC.
The breach is a setback for an industry that is maturing and seeking to expand into traditional finance. Before now, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost US$1.5 billion in tokens.
Notorious previous episodes of theft and fraud among fallen crypto giants such as FTX and Mt Gox set the stage for protracted bear markets, bruises the industry has worked to put behind it in US President Donald Trump’s promised new era of regulatory clarity for cryptocurrencies.
Largest token Bitcoin fell on news of the Binance attack, dropping below US$77,000 for the first time in more than a month. It pared losses later, trading at around US$77,500 at 6 am in New York.
For crypto faithful who had been basking in a two-month-long price rebound, the Binance incident has cast a shadow over the recovery.
“Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive officer and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data.
Binance dwarfs its industry rivals. It holds roughly US$135.2 billion in assets, compared with US$28.6 billion at the second-largest exchange OKX, according to DefiLlama data.
The hackers appear to have exploited how Binance authorises transactions, according to TRM. They seemingly gained access to the exchange’s systems and used internal software to authorise transfers across 10 different blockchains, including Bitcoin and Ethereum, it said.
“TRM attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, North Korea’s elite hacking unit, based on robust on and off-chain intelligence,” the firm added. “We make this judgment with high confidence.”
Binance said that the incident may involve a compromised software engineer’s laptop, among “additional points of breach”. It found no evidence of leaked private keys, it revealed. “This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it,” Binance posted on X.
An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve as a backstop for customers in “extreme situations”, according to the exchange. The SAFU is generally maintained at around US$1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024.
The two biggest stablecoin issuers said that they took steps to freeze affected currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than US$1.5 billion of the stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack”. Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group, said that US$800 million of its coin had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance”.
Sentiment was already fragile after a spate of crypto security incidents. In recent months, hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget, while tampering involving Ledger devices also led to millions of dollars in losses.
“Attackers are operating at unprecedented speed and scale” but “the tools to track and trace operate at that speed too”, said Ari Redbord, global head of policy at TRM Labs. “Stablecoin issuers freeze within hours. Investigators follow funds across chains in real time.”
Traders had already been bracing for greater volatility in the crypto market this week, with US$11 billion in options set to expire Friday. This comes days ahead of the US midterm elections taking place next week, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry.
Exchange thefts and malfeasance have been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt Gox was struck in 2011. Over time, the hackers made off with tokens worth billions of dollars based on the current market price. Mt Gox eventually went bankrupt.
“It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.”
The Binance incident came on the same day event-contract venue Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after it said that a third-party software provider was compromised. More than 700 Polymarket users were drained of US$2.7 million in funds, said blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps, in a post on X. A spokesman declined to comment on the numbers.
South Korea’s second-largest crypto exchange Bithumb was also among the country’s finance firms hit by data breaches this week, with hundreds of customer records affected, Yonhap reported.ng as crypto’s biggest-ever hack. Digital tokens fell. BLOOMBERG

sources.news_title: Binance crypto exchange confirms major hack, more than $2.5 billion frozen
sources.text:
The international cryptocurrency platform has temporarily frozen all deposits and withdrawals following a likely hack, the biggest on record so far, which crypto security firms are saying could have originated in North Korea.
“Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating,” Binance posted on social media early morning India time on September 30. “User funds are completely safe.”
“Binance will cover all losses. As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement,” the company said in a subsequent post.
The company further said that the current verified total amount of funds that have been frozen is $3 billion.
“This figure may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” it added.
The impact of the announcements on the price of Bitcoin was immediate, with the cryptocurrency falling 6% to trade at around $76,500 by Friday morning.
How the attack played out
According to crypto security firm TRM Labs, attackers siphoned off approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, with most of the money stolen in about 20 minutes starting at 1.35 AM Indian Standard Time (IST).
“That makes this the largest crypto theft on record, about four times the $1.5 billion Bybit hack of February 2025,” TRM Labs said in a post on the attack.
The security firm attributes the attack to TraderTraitor, a major hacking network operating out of North Korea.
“We base this assessment on robust on and off-chain intelligence sources,” TRM Labs said. “The FBI named the same group as responsible for the USD 1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025.”
“Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack and the KelpDAO hack in April 2026: small Tornado Cash withdrawals funding an operator wallet, staging that began well before the theft, and signatures obtained in advance then executed in one burst,” it added.
It did, however, say that the pattern of laundering the stolen cryptocurrencies differs in this case from how it was done following the Bybit hack.

sources.news_title: Binance freezes $3 billion in assets after suspected hack
sources.text:
Hackers stole $6.3 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack ever.
The attack could prompt investors to rethink the risks of owning digital assets.
The hackers behind the raid were from North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.
The attackers targeted Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and shifted most of the funds in about 20 minutes, TRM Labs said in a statement.
Binance has said that it was working to resolve a "complex attack" which involved several "points of breach".
"Our initial investigation suggested that the security incident may have involved a compromised laptop, however our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach," the firm wrote on X.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it."
It said that it worked with partners to freeze the affected assets with about $3bn located so far.
However Binance did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3bn, and its co-founder Yi He said the exchange would cover "all hacking losses".
Crypto prices fall as Binance sees $6.3bn security breach
Binance said its deposits were unaffected and it expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours.
TRM said several features of the attack matched earlier heists linked to North Korea, including a 2025 hack of crypto-exchange Bybit that the US Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang.
"We make this judgment with high confidence," it said in a statement.
North Korea's mission in Geneva and its embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
The incident could be the world's biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.
"It's the biggest hack in history," said Aravind Srinivasan, head of large crypto market maker GSR's systematic OTC business.
Markets reacted immediately in Asian trading today.
Bitcoin dropped more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368 and Ether fell more than 3% to a two-month low of $2,178.
BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5% over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to market aggregator CoinGecko.
Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global slid 4.8% while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy fell nearly 6% in extended US trading.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has more than 335 million registered users globally and had about $160bn in assets under custody as of the exchange's 2024 annual report.
An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of its engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorised withdrawals, Binance said.
"The incident stems from multiple factors. Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident," Binance said.
Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher US interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said.
"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralised exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks," said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8bn in assets under custody as of the exchange's 2025 annual report.
"User funds remain safe," Binance said in a statement.
Binance runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website.
"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them," said Bernardo Brites, CEO of Trace Finance, a payments and stablecoin infrastructure company.
"My view is that users will move away from smaller and medium-sized exchanges, (it is) becoming too risky to park your money somewhere that couldn't cover a hack of meaningful size."
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57bn in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800m.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said yesterday it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack.
Binance's Yi said $27m in stablecoins and about $2m worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200m in funds, Mr Yi said.
Jack McDonald, senior vice president of stablecoins at Ripple, said the company was closely monitoring reports of a potential exploit involving Binance and was freezing affected funds and coordinating with relevant parties.
Miguel Morel, CEO of blockchain intelligence firm Arkham, said data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been hacked from Binance by an unknown actor.
The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9bn worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs.
In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350m in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry's vulnerability to hackers.
Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.
Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.
Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.
In an unrelated incident earlier yesterday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

sources.news_title: Binance reports $6.3 billion crypto breach, potentially the biggest hack in history
sources.text:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance said Friday that a security breach had an estimated impact of $6.3 billion, potentially making it the largest cryptocurrency hack in history, as the company raced to freeze stolen assets, suspended deposits and withdrawals, and sought to reassure customers that their funds remained safe.
The world's largest cryptocurrency exchange said approximately $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen with the help of blockchain partners. The status of the remaining $3.3 billion was not immediately clear, while Binance co-founder Yi He pledged that the company would cover all losses resulting from the attack.
An initial investigation suggested that hackers may have gained access through a compromised laptop belonging to a Binance DevOps engineer. According to the company, the breach allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
Binance stressed that investigators had found no evidence that cryptocurrency wallet private keys, the credentials used to control digital assets, had been exposed. It said a full technical report would be published once the investigation was completed.
The exchange temporarily suspended all deposits and withdrawals, revoked the affected address authorization and enlisted law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence specialists to trace the funds. It also promised to publish updated proof of reserves after completing its security measures.
Bitcoin plunges as crypto markets react
The suspected attack sent shock waves through cryptocurrency markets in early Asian trading Friday.
Bitcoin fell more than 3% to a six-week low of $76,368, while ether dropped more than 3% to $2,178, its lowest level in two months. Binance's BNB token declined 5% over 24 hours to $709.70, according to cryptocurrency market tracker CoinGecko.
The selloff also spread to cryptocurrency-related stocks. Shares of Coinbase Global fell 4.8% in extended U.S. trading, while Strategy, the company known for its large Bitcoin holdings, dropped nearly 6%.
Blockchain analytics company Chainalysis and other industry experts said the incident could become the largest cryptocurrency heist ever recorded.
"It's the biggest hack in history," said Aravind Srinivasan, head of systematic over-the-counter trading at major cryptocurrency market maker GSR.
The breach comes at a difficult time for digital assets, which have already faced pressure from higher U.S. interest rates and weaker demand from buyers of cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds.
"It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges, as well as counterparty, solvency and liquidity risks," said Tim Sun, a senior researcher at Hong Kong-based HashKey Group.
Binance has approximately 335 million registered users worldwide and held about $162.8 billion in assets under custody, according to its 2025 annual report.
Billions frozen as Binance promises to cover losses
Several major cryptocurrency companies moved to freeze assets linked to the breach.
Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets, while rival Circle froze more than $800 million. Ripple also froze approximately $200 million, according to Yi He.
World Liberty Financial, a cryptocurrency company linked to President Donald Trump and his family, said it had worked with digital asset custodian BitGo to freeze funds associated with the attack. Yi said approximately $27 million in stablecoins and another $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen.
Binance said it would compensate customers using its Secure Asset Fund for Users, known as SAFU, alongside company funds. The reserve, held entirely in Bitcoin, is intended to protect customers against losses from security incidents.
"User funds remain safe," Binance said, adding that the precautionary suspension of deposits and withdrawals would continue while security teams reviewed the exchange's infrastructure.
The company did not provide a timetable for restoring normal operations.
Security experts warned that the incident could have consequences far beyond the immediate financial losses.
"It's becoming very hard to counter hacks as AI can find vulnerabilities faster than you can fix them," said Bernardo Brites, chief executive of payments and stablecoin infrastructure company Trace Finance.
Brites predicted that the breach could accelerate a shift away from smaller cryptocurrency exchanges, which may lack the financial resources to absorb a major cyberattack.
Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was unaffected by the incident. Coinbase also said its operations had not been affected and that it was monitoring developments.
A potentially record-breaking cryptocurrency theft
Blockchain intelligence company Arkham said transaction data indicated that billions of dollars appeared to have been taken from Binance by an unidentified attacker.
The incident follows a series of major cryptocurrency thefts that have raised concerns about the industry's security. According to blockchain research firm TRM Labs, hackers stole $2.9 billion in cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks last year.
In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget reported that approximately $350 million in digital assets had been stolen from its platform.
Authorities have also warned that organized criminal networks increasingly exploit cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside conventional banking systems.
In a separate incident Thursday, prediction market platform Polymarket temporarily halted trading following a security breach involving a third-party provider. Trading later resumed, with the company promising to reimburse affected users.
For Binance, the immediate priorities remain identifying the attackers, tracing the remaining assets and restoring access to customer accounts. The exchange has promised to cover losses, but the ultimate financial cost and how much of the affected cryptocurrency can be recovered remain uncertain.

sources.news_title: Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5bn frozen
sources.text:
Crypto platform Binance confirms 'complex' $6.3 bn hack
New York (AFP) – Cryptocurrency platform Binance said Friday it was working to resolve a "complex attack" that affected around $6.3 billion in funds, in what is thought to be the biggest ever crypto heist, with investigators pointing to hackers linked to North Korea.
Issued on: Modified:
Blockchain investigation firm TRM Labs said it had "high confidence" that the attack was orchestrated by a North Korea-affiliated group called TraderTraitor, the same group blamed for the $1.5 billion theft from the Bybit platform in February last year.
Another analytics firm, Elliptic, also attributed the attack to North Korea-linked hackers, according to industry outlet CoinDesk.
TraderTraitor is believed to be part of Lazarus Group, which gained notoriety in 2014 when it was accused of hacking into Sony Pictures as revenge for "The Interview," a film that mocked North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
Binance, the world's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volumes, said investigations had "uncovered additional points of breach," contrary to initial findings that suggested the hack involved a single compromised laptop.
"This was a complex attack, and we are doing all we can in coordination with law enforcement to resolve it," Binance wrote on X.
The company confirmed on its X account for Latin America that "the total estimated impact is around $6.3 billion," four times the amount taken in the Bybit hack, the biggest cyberattack of its kind until now.
Binance warned the figure "may continue to increase as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets."
It said around $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen.
Customers' account balances have not been touched, but they cannot move funds off the platform while withdrawals remain suspended.
Binance initially suspended all deposits and withdrawals but later said deposits were unaffected. At about 0900 GMT Friday, it said it was on track to resume withdrawals in 45 hours.
President Donald Trump said Friday the United States was looking into the hack, and the FBI said it was "engaged with relevant public and private partners to understand the scope of the activity" and was ready to investigate.
Fund freeze
The company had said on X that initial investigation suggested the hack involved a compromised laptop belonging to a "DevOps engineer," allowing the unauthorized party to execute unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
"We have found no evidence of any private key leaks from wallets," it said, promising to share a detailed technical analysis once investigations were complete.
The unauthorized withdrawals drained Binance's hot wallets -- the online wallets the exchange uses to process customer transfers -- across several blockchains, according to CoinDesk.
Binance earlier posted a series of sometimes contradictory messages, insisting that "user funds are completely safe" but also saying it would "cover all losses."
Paolo Ardoino, the boss of Tether, a company that issues a cryptocurrency known as USDT, said his firm froze about $1.6 billion "related to a potential Binance exchange hack."
Jeremy Allaire, who runs cryptocurrency platform Circle, said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC.
USDT and USDC are both "stablecoins," or digital currencies whose value is linked to a traditional currency, the US dollar.
Crypto prices tumble
For several hours before Binance confirmed the attack, industry observers said hackers had managed to reach the platform.
The prices of most major cryptocurrencies fell on news of the cyberattack, except for the stablecoins, which by definition can only fluctuate within tight margins.
Bitcoin plunged nearly five percent after the news, falling overnight to around $76,400, its lowest level since mid-September, before recovering slightly to trade at about $77,300.
Ethereum dropped nearly six percent, while BNB, native to Binance, tumbled nearly 10 percent.
The attack on Binance comes as many observers express worries that the ever-expanding capabilities of artificial intelligence (AI) models could compromise cryptography and IT security protocols.

sources.news_title: Binance Hack Fears: $2.5B Frozen, Bitcoin Below $78,000
sources.text:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Friday that a "complex attack" had drained an estimated $6.3 billion in digital assets from its wallets, confirming the largest theft in the industry's history roughly 12 hours after billions of dollars began moving out of its hot wallets and it suspended withdrawals across every network it serves. About $3 billion of the stolen assets had been frozen on-chain with the help of stablecoin issuers and blockchain partners, the exchange said, and it repeated its pledge to cover all customer losses.
The exchange stopped short of using the word. "Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," a Binance spokesperson said. "Rest assured that user funds are completely safe." Within an hour the company had revised its statement twice, and spokesperson Ross O'Leary told reporters that Binance had "temporarily suspended withdrawals on multiple networks following a security incident as a precautionary measure." Trading on Binance Alpha, its platform for early-stage tokens, was also paused. Shortly after midnight UTC the exchange went further. "Binance will cover all losses," it said in a post on its official X account, announcing that all deposits and withdrawals were suspended "while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement." It promised a full post-mortem once the investigation is complete and said its U.S. affiliate, Binance.US, was not affected. By Friday morning the hedging was gone. "The total estimated impact is around $6.3 billion," Binance said, warning that the figure "may continue to increase" as its teams worked with law enforcement, issuers and blockchain intelligence firms to trace and freeze further assets. At about 9 a.m. GMT it said it was on track to resume withdrawals within 45 hours; co-founder Yi He said she expected them back by Sunday.
Changpeng Zhao, who founded Binance and stepped down as chief executive in 2023 after pleading guilty to U.S. anti-money-laundering charges, was blunter than the company he no longer runs. "It does look like a hack on Binance," he wrote on X, adding that as a shareholder he expected all user funds to be fully covered. Co-founder Yi He said withdrawals would stay closed until the exchange's environment was confirmed safe.
The scale of what left the wallets was contested for most of Thursday night before Binance's own figure settled it. The security firm Blockaid had identified roughly $3.3 billion in suspicious transfers across Ethereum, Arbitrum and Avalanche; Arkham put the attacker's holdings above $5.7 billion once bitcoin, ether and other networks were added; Chainalysis estimated about $5.9 billion. TRM Labs, after the exchange's confirmation, said an attacker moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets on ten blockchains, most of it in about 20 minutes. The previous record was the $1.5 billion taken from the Bybit exchange in February 2025 by hackers linked to North Korea's Lazarus Group, and TRM said several features of Thursday's attack matched earlier North Korea-linked heists, assessing that a North Korean unit was likely responsible. Binance has not attributed the attack.
What distinguishes this incident from Bybit is the speed of the response from the companies that control the plumbing. Tether, the issuer of the USDT stablecoin, froze more than $1.567 billion of its tokens connected to the suspected breach, chief executive Paolo Ardoino said. Circle froze more than $800 million in USDC and said it was coordinating with law enforcement. Binance said overnight that the verified total frozen stood at $2.54 billion, and by Friday morning put it at about $3 billion, describing the response as "an industry-wide effort" and saying the number would keep rising as issuers and intelligence firms traced further assets.
Stablecoins can be frozen because their issuers retain the ability to blacklist addresses, a centralized feature that the crypto industry has long debated and that has repeatedly proved decisive in limiting hack losses. The attacker's most liquid assets were therefore locked first. Bitcoin and ether cannot be frozen in the same way, and on-chain trackers reported that the attacker was already routing funds through decentralized exchanges in an effort to convert or obscure them before further blacklisting could catch up. Roughly $700 million in USDT and $445 million in ether were reported to have moved before or outside the freeze.
Markets reacted immediately. Bitcoin fell about 3 percent to below $78,000, briefly touching $77,800, and ether dropped 4 percent to around $2,250. More than $1 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated over 24 hours, including more than $600 million in a single hour as the news spread. The sell-off reflects less a fear that the underlying assets are compromised, since the blockchains themselves were not breached, than the possibility that an exchange handling a large share of global trading volume could face a solvency question if the final loss exceeds its reserves. Binance's own token, BNB, fell nearly 10 percent before recovering about 2.7 percent on Friday.
On that point Binance has one cushion that smaller exchanges lack. Its Secure Asset Fund for Users, an emergency reserve established in 2018, holds about $1 billion, denominated in bitcoin since early this year. Whether that fund can absorb the loss depends on a number Binance has not yet disclosed: the net shortfall after freezes. If the $6.3 billion estimate holds and about $3 billion is recovered, the gap would exceed the fund, and the pledge to cover all losses would have to be met from the exchange's own balance sheet. That arithmetic will be the central question for depositors when withdrawals reopen.
Binance's first account of the cause pointed to a single machine. Its initial investigation, it said, suggested that a laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer had been compromised, giving the attacker access to a "service container" from which unauthorized withdrawal transactions could be executed; a subsequent investigation, it said on Friday, "uncovered additional points of breach." It said it had found no evidence that any wallet private key had leaked and promised a detailed technical analysis when the probe is complete. Hot wallets, which hold the funds an exchange needs for day-to-day withdrawals, are connected to the internet and are the standard target for exchange thefts; the Bybit attack began with a compromised developer workstation at a third-party wallet provider that allowed the attackers to alter a transaction the exchange's signers believed was routine. Binance has not said whether it received any communication from the attackers. Its only confirmed prior exchange breach, in May 2019, cost about 7,000 bitcoin, then worth around $40 million.
The Binance incident was the second security event to hit a major crypto platform Thursday. Hours earlier, the prediction market Polymarket halted trading and paused withdrawals after confirming that a third-party provider had been compromised. Security researchers traced the breach to a monitoring script supplied by a vendor called DebugBear, which was altered to drain user wallets; losses were estimated at between $2 million and $2.7 million. Polymarket said all affected customers would be reimbursed and resumed trading later in the day. The two incidents are not known to be connected.
Unlike bank deposits, funds held on cryptocurrency exchanges carry no government insurance in the United States or most other jurisdictions, leaving any reimbursement to the exchange's discretion and balance sheet. Binance said it would publish updates only through its official channels once information was verified, and that withdrawals would resume within about 45 hours of its Friday morning update.

sources.news_title: Binance Security Breach Triggers USD 3 Billion Freeze, Deposits and Withdrawals Suspended
Potential Binance 'hack' forces crypto firms to freeze $3 billion
Bombshell after $9 billion stolen in 20 mins
Crypto platform Binance confirms major hack, more than $2.5B in funds frozen
Binance and Polymarket are investigating potential hacks. The former says it's frozen around $3 billion.
sources.text:
Two major trading platforms — Binance and Polymarket — were investigating security incidents on Thursday, with the former facing potential losses in the billions. There's no evidence the incidents were related.
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading volume, said it was actively investigating reports of a "potential security issue."
In an update late Thursday, Binance said that its initial investigation suggested that the incident may involve a compromised development operations engineer's laptop. This allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions.
"We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak," the company added.
Binance said the estimated total impact is about $6.3 billion, and it has worked with its blockchain partners to freeze around $3 billion in assets so far.
"Deposits remain unaffected and continue to operate as normal," Binance wrote on X early Friday morning. "Withdrawals remain paused while our team completes a security revamp of the withdrawal service and its related addresses. We expect to resume within 48 hours."
The company previously said on X that it would cover all losses and suspended both deposits and withdrawals while it conducted security checks.
The company did not respond to a request for comment.
Binance founder and former CEO, Changpeng Zhao, said on X a hack seemed likely.
“User funds are safe! It does look like a hack on Binance,” Zhao wrote in a post on X. “I don't manage Binance anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”
Zhao expressed appreciation to Tether and Circle, issuers of cryptocurrencies traded on Binance, for quickly freezing funds.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X the company froze more than $1.5 billion related to the potential Binance hack. Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company froze over $800 million in connection with the incident and that it was coordinating with law enforcement.
Polymarket also reported a security incident
Also on Thursday, Polymarket, the world's largest prediction market by trading volume, temporarily halted trading after users reported unauthorized withdrawals.
The company said in a statement on X that one of its third-party providers was compromised and that the incident had been referred to law enforcement. It also said trading had resumed by 3 p.m. Eastern time.
A Polymarket spokesperson told Business Insider that the malicious activity occurred in the UK and that the company will reimburse affected users. The company was unable to confirm the amount that may have been stolen.
Polymarket's US exchange was not halted and did not appear to be affected.
A person familiar with the matter attributed the Polymarket hack to a compromised third-party provider called DebugBear, a web performance monitoring platform designed to help businesses optimize website speed. It's unclear exactly how Polymarket uses the platform.
DebugBear did not respond to a request for comment. The company said in an X post on Thursday that it was aware of a security incident and was treating it as a "top priority."

sources.news_title: Binance Hack May Involve Key Misuse, Not Theft: Blockaid
sources.text:
The suspected multi-billion-dollar Binance hack may have involved attackers manipulating the exchange’s transaction-signing signature rather than stealing private keys, according to Blockaid co-founder and CEO Ido Ben-Natan.
Speaking to Cointelegraph, Ben-Natan said Blockaid’s preliminary assessment pointed to “key misuse,” in which attackers trick or compromise a signing system into authorizing malicious transactions without extracting the underlying private key.
“It seems to be… a compromise of signing infrastructure. We don’t think a key was leaked,” he said.
Ben-Natan said this was a preliminary assessment, drawing on their experience with similar attacks and their observations of the onchain activity.
Binance has not confirmed the precise method that allowed hackers to steal over $2.5 billion in crypto from the exchange — the largest crypto hack in history.
Arkham CEO Miguel Morel told Cointelegraph there isn’t enough information at this point in time to confirm whether the attack involved stolen keys or compromised infrastructure.
“From what we can tell, it appears the hack is still ongoing,” he said.
Related: Binance hack rattles crypto markets as BNB falls 7%, Bitcoin slides
Blockaid identifies malicious wallet delegation
In its onchain analysis published on X, Blockaid said the attacker bundled 50 EIP-7702 authorizations into a single transaction targeting Binance 14. One authorization reportedly matched the account’s required nonce, allowing it to be accepted.
EIP-7702 allows an account to delegate execution to smart-contract code. Blockaid said the affected account was delegated to an unverified sweeper contract that allowed a designated operator to drain tokens and Ether.
Ben-Natan told Cointelegraph the operation could have involved multiple compromised devices and movement through the exchange’s network, though this remains unconfirmed.
North Korea, Bybit comparison
Asked whether the suspected signing manipulation resembled the February 2025 Bybit attack, Ben-Natan described the incidents as “very, very similar.”
In that case, Bybit’s published forensic update said attackers compromised a Safe developer’s credentials, accessed the wallet provider’s infrastructure and deceived signers into approving a malicious transaction.
Like Bybit, Ben-Natan said the activity resembled operations linked to North Korean cyber attackers, based on the sophistication of the on-chain preparations.
Magazine: Tampered Ledger reported in Singapore a month before news broke: Asia Express
Source: Coin Telegraph

sources.news_title: Binance freezes $2.5 billion after suspected hack; Bitcoin sinks below $79,000
sources.text:
A suspected hack of Binance, the world’s largest crypto exchange, prompted it to freeze more than $2.5 billion in assets and sent the price of digital tokens tumbling. Binance said it hasn’t confirmed any impact to customer funds.
“We are aware of reports of a potential security issue and we are actively investigating,” a Binance spokesperson said. “At this stage, we have not confirmed any impact to user funds. Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information.”
Still, Binance said it has currently frozen $2.54 billion in assets and may raise that figure further as its teams work with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners.
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao said the exchange may have been hacked but he expects all user funds will be fully covered. Zhao, who goes by CZ, no longer runs the company but remains its largest shareholder.
Online forums were rife with loss estimates and theories of how the attack was designed, none of them confirmed. Blockchain tracker Arkham has identified wallets associated with the suspected hacker holding about $5.9 billion in digital assets, though the figure does not necessarily represent the amount stolen from Binance.
Bitcoin slumped as much as 3.7% — falling below $79,000 to its lowest level since September — with other tokens also selling off. US stocks ended lower, with the Nasdaq 100 tech index dropping nearly 1.4%.
“The rumored Binance hack is definitely driving down coin prices,” said Fredrick Collins, chief executive and co-founder of crypto data platform Velo Data. “Binance is such a behemoth in crypto that any hit to confidence in them is a hit to confidence in the industry as a whole, especially as people have already been skittish over the increasing cyber capabilities of AI.”
For crypto faithful who’d been basking in a two-month-long price rebound amid the tightening embrace of institutional Wall Street, the incident is a potential setback. Notorious episodes of theft and fraud among fallen crypto giants such as FTX and Mt. Gox set the stage for protracted bear markets in the past, bruises the industry has worked to put behind it in US President Donald Trump’s promised new era of regulatory clarity for cryptocurrencies.
To date, the biggest publicly known crypto hack occurred at exchange Bybit in February 2025, in which attackers made off with almost $1.5 billion of tokens.
Binance said it has suspended withdrawals on multiple networks. “This is a precautionary measure and we are working to restore services as soon as it is safe to do so,” the company said in a statement.
An emergency insurance and reserve fund from Binance called the Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) was established in 2018 to serve a backstop for customers in “extreme situations,” according to the exchange. The SAFU fund is generally maintained at around $1 billion, but has fluctuated in the past in tandem with market movements, Binance said in 2024.
The two biggest stablecoin issuers said they took steps to freeze missing currency. Paolo Ardoino, the chief executive officer of Tether, said in an X post that it froze more than $1.5 billion of the stablecoin “related to a potential Binance exchange hack.” Jeremy Allaire, who runs Circle Internet Group Inc., said $800 million of its coin had been frozen amid “reports of a potential exploit involving Binance.”
“Hot wallets getting drained is not something new to crypto, but the amount would be a meaningful hack on the largest crypto exchange,” said James Seyffart at Bloomberg Intelligence. “It’s definitely a bad look. And this is one after another,” he said of a recent spate of security incidents.
Already fragile sentiment was hit further after a bruising run of crypto security incidents. In recent months, hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget, while tampering tied to Ledger devices also led to millions of dollars in losses.
Traders had already been bracing for greater volatility in the crypto market this week, with $11 billion in options set to expire Friday. This comes days ahead of the US midterm elections taking place next week, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry.
Exchange thefts and malfeasance has been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was struck in 2011. Over time, the hackers made off with tokens worth billions of dollars based on the current market price. Mt. Gox eventually went bankrupt.
“It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.”
The incident came on the same day event-contract venue Polymarket halted trading on its international exchange for an hour after it said that a third-party software provider was compromised. More than 700 Polymarket users were drained of $2.7 million in funds, said blockchain analytics platform Bubblemaps, in a post on X. A spokesman declined to comment on the numbers.

sources.news_title: Binance’s possible hack triggers US$3 billion freeze in crypto assets
sources.text: SINGAPORE/TOKYO -- Hackers stole US$6.3 billion from Binance, the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchange, in a record theft that analysts pinned on North Korea and said could shake faith in digital assets. Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial. The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. TRM said the attackers were able to order wallets that Binance uses to empty into hacker-controlled wallets, mirroring a 2025 heist at crypto exchange Bybit, which the U.S. Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang. “TRM attributes the attack to ... North Korea’s elite hacking unit,” the firm said in an analysis of the hack posted to its website. Both TRM and Chainalysis said they were highly confident North Korea was responsible. ‘Biggest hack in history’ North Korea has for years used state-linked cyber units for espionage, financial theft and revenue, according to U.S. and South Korean authorities as well as cybersecurity experts. North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters’ requests for comment. Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours. It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion. “Your money is safe and we’re covering every loss,” co-CEO Richard Teng said on X. “Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual.” “It’s the biggest hack in history,” Aravind Srinivasan at market maker GSR said as crypto prices fell broadly. Bitcoin hit a six-week low of $76,368 and ether ETH= fell more than 3 per cent to a two-month low of $2,178 before markets stabilized. BNB, a token originally launched as Binance Coin that can be used to pay Binance fees, was down 5 per cent over the past 24 hours at $709.70, according to CoinGecko, while shaky confidence hit listed crypto exchange shares. Shares in crypto exchange Coinbase Global, which said it was unaffected, slid 4.8 per cent, while those of bitcoin buyer Strategy MSTR.O fell nearly 6 per cent in extended U.S. trading. Compromised laptop An initial investigation suggested the breach may have started with a hacked laptop belonging to one of Binance’s engineers, which let an attacker gain access to one of its systems and make unauthorized withdrawals, Binance said. “Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident,” Binance said. Mark Karpeles, former chief of defunct Tokyo-based bitcoin exchange Mt Gox, which collapsed a dozen years ago after $500 million in bitcoin was stolen, said attackers probably accessed private keys for at least two Binance wallets. “Binance appears to have split its assets across multiple systems, ensuring a hack can only affect a part of the assets, but even so a single hack is a large loss,” he said. Beyond the potential loss of assets, the security breach was likely to have wider ramifications for crypto, which had already been under pressure due to higher U.S. interest rates and softer demand from exchange-traded fund buyers, analysts said. “It may further dampen risk appetite and prompt investors to reassess the safety of assets held on centralized exchanges,” said Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey Group, based in Hong Kong. Hack size tops Binance secure asset fund Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has 335 million registered users globally and had about $162.8 billion in assets under custody as of the exchange’s 2025 annual report. The crypto exchange runs a secure asset fund for users, which is a $1 billion reserve held entirely in bitcoin that is intended to protect user assets in cases of security breaches, according to its website. Co-CEO Teng said that “and company funds” will cover losses. Stablecoin issuer Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million. World Liberty Financial said it worked with custodian BitGo to freeze funds, and Binance co-founder Yi He said $27 million in stablecoins and about $2 million worth of World Liberty tokens had been frozen. Crypto firm Ripple also froze roughly $200 million in funds, Yi said. The incident adds to a string of crypto thefts. Last year, attackers stole $2.9 billion worth of cryptocurrency across nearly 150 attacks, according to researchers at TRM Labs. In September, cryptocurrency exchange Bitget said roughly $350 million in crypto had been stolen from its platform, underscoring the industry’s vulnerability to hackers. Reporting by Tom Westbrook, Ankur Banerjee and Rae Wee in Singapore, Summer Zhen in Hong Kong, Rocky Swift in Tokyo, Vallari Srivastava and Anusha Shah in Bengaluru and Mrinmay Dey in Mexico City; Writing by Scott Murdoch and Tom Westbrook; Editing by Jamie Freed, Stephen Coates and Jan Harvey, Reuters
