sources.news_title: World's largest crypto exchange Binance freezes $2.54 billion after suspected hack
sources.text:
Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a potential security breach that could have affected assets worth around $6.3 billion, the company said on Thursday. However, it has not confirmed whether funds were stolen or established the full extent of the damage.
Blockchain analysis firm TRM said North Korea was behind the $6 billion crypto hack on Binance.
The exchange said it was working to resolve the issue and had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while conducting security checks and coordinating with law enforcement and industry partners.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement, adding that its security teams were reviewing all relevant information and would provide updates through official channels once the details were verified.
In a post on X, Binance said its estimated total impact stood at around $6.3 billion, with roughly $3 billion in affected assets frozen on the blockchain so far. The company added that it was working with blockchain partners to trace and freeze additional funds.
Binance's initial investigation suggested that the incident may have involved a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop, which allegedly allowed an attacker to access a service container and submit unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
The exchange said it had found no evidence of a wallet private key leak. It added that further technical details would be released after the investigation was completed and the findings fully verified.
Tether, Circle freeze funds linked to incident
Stablecoin issuers Tether and Circle have also frozen assets associated with the potential breach.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.5 billion in assets linked to what he described as a potential Binance exchange hack. Circle co-founder and CEO Jeremy Allaire said the company had frozen more than $800 million in associated funds in coordination with law enforcement.
Binance said it was working with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.
Changpeng Zhao, Binance's founder who stepped down as CEO in 2023, also described the incident as a possible hack in a post on X.
“User funds are safe!” Zhao wrote, adding that although he no longer managed Binance, he expected all user funds to be fully covered as a shareholder.
The incident has also coincided with pressure on cryptocurrency markets. Bitcoin fell 3.2% on Thursday evening, slipping below $79,000.
Binance investigates possible access through employee laptop
The suspected compromise of a DevOps engineer's laptop has emerged as a key line of inquiry. According to Binance's preliminary assessment, the attacker may have used access to a service container to initiate unauthorised withdrawals.
The company has not confirmed the identity of the attacker or established whether the incident resulted in a loss of user funds. It said it would release more technical information after verifying the facts.
The episode adds to persistent security concerns in the cryptocurrency industry, where exchanges and other platforms remain targets for cyberattacks and unauthorised transactions.
Founded in 2017, Binance allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets and has grown into the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange. Zhao stepped down as CEO in 2023 after pleading guilty to a felony related to failures to prevent money laundering on the platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday that $2.54 billion in crypto assets had been frozen as it investigated a potential security breach, with stablecoin issuers Circle CRCL.N and Tether freezing related assets.
"Binance will cover all hacking losses," Binance co-founder Yi He said.
Binance said the amount frozen could increase as it worked with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.

Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.

Binance freezes assets after record $6.3-billion heist. Reuters
Hackers stole $6.3-billion from Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, in what analysts say is the biggest crypto hack ever, an attack that could prompt investors to rethink the risks of owning digital assets.
The hackers behind the raid were from North Korea, according to U.S. blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis. The attackers targeted Binance wallets on 10 blockchains and shifted most of the funds in about 20 minutes, TRM Labs said in a statement.

TRM said several features of the attack matched earlier heists linked to North Korea, including a 2025 hack of crypto exchange Bybit that the US Federal Bureau of Investigation had attributed to Pyongyang.
“We make this judgment with high confidence,” it said in a statement.
Gone in 20 minutes: How the biggest heist in crypto history unfolded at Binance
North Korea’s mission in Geneva and its embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment.
The incident could be the world’s biggest crypto heist, according to analytics firm Chainalysis and other industry experts.

INCIDENT ADDS TO STRING OF CRYPTO THEFTS

Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange, said on Thursday that $2.54 billion in crypto assets had been frozen as it investigated a potential security breach, with stablecoin issuers Circle and Tether freezing related assets.
"Binance will cover all hacking losses," Binance co-founder Yi He said.
Binance said the amount frozen could increase as it worked with law enforcement agencies, token issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and other industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.
Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, who no longer runs the company, said in a post on X that the incident "looked like a hack."
Tether said it had frozen nearly $1.57 billion in assets linked to the incident, while Circle froze more than $800 million.
Binance said it was conducting security checks and would resume withdrawals once the issue was fully resolved. It added user funds remained safe and that teams were reviewing the incident.
The exchange also temporarily suspended trading on its Binance Alpha platform as a precaution.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it had worked with cryptocurrency custodian BitGo to freeze funds stolen in what it described as a Binance hack. Authorities have warned that organised crime groups are increasingly using cryptocurrencies to move funds across borders outside the traditional financial system.
Binance, which allows users to buy, sell and trade digital assets, has more than 300 million registered users globally and about $160 billion in assets under custody, according to the exchange's 2024 annual report.
Binance.US, a separate cryptocurrency exchange, said it was not affected by the security incident.
Coinbase said it was unaffected and was monitoring the situation.
In an unrelated incident earlier on Thursday, prediction market operator Polymarket temporarily halted trading after a security incident involving a third-party provider. It later resumed trading and said it would fully reimburse affected traders.

Binance crypto exchange suspends trades over North Korea-linked hack
October 30, 2026
Blockchain analysts said a North Korean hacking unit was likely behind the theft of more than $6 billion from Binance, the world's largest cryptocurrency exchange.
Binance temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals for security checks and said about $3 billion in affected assets had been frozen.
US-based blockchain intelligence firm TRM attributed the attack to TraderTraitor, which it described as an elite North Korean hacking unit.
"We make this judgment with high confidence," TRM said in a report published Thursday.
Why do analysts suspect North Korea?
TRM said attackers moved approximately $6.36 billion out of Binance wallets across 10 blockchains, most of it within about 20 minutes. It described the incident as the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
"Several features of this attack match earlier North Korea-linked heists, including the Bybit hack," the firm said.
Bybit lost $1.5 billion in a hack in February 2025. The FBI attributed that attack to North Korea and TraderTraitor.
Jonathan Levin, co-founder and CEO of blockchain analysis company Chainalysis, also said the Binance attack was likely carried out by TraderTraitor.
Experts say North Korea uses cryptocurrency theft and other illicit cyber activities to obtain foreign currency and help fund its nuclear program despite international sanctions.
What has Binance said about the hack?
Binance did not confirm the attribution to North Korea, saying it was "working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of the criminals and bring them to justice."
Binance said it worked to secure the affected assets and that it had located and frozen about $3 billion (€2.7 billion) so far. It did not provide information about the remaining $3.3 billion.
"Binance will cover all hacking losses," co-founder Yi He said, without providing more details about the incident.
"Rest assured that user funds are completely safe," a company spokesperson said.
Binance said its initial investigation suggested an attacker had compromised a software infrastructure engineer's laptop, gaining access to an internal service and submitting unauthorized withdrawals. The company said it had found no evidence that wallet private keys had leaked.
Tether froze around $1.6 billion in its USDT currency, according to CEO Paolo Ardoino, and Circle froze some $800 million-worth of USDC, boss Jeremy Allaire said.
The news of the possible hack sent Bitcoin's value tumbling by 3.2% on Thursday evening, dropping below $79,000.
Who is Binance ex-CEO Zhao?
Zhao, who founded the Binance platform in 2017, said "as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered."
He stepped down as CEO after pleading guilty in 2023. to failing to prevent money laundering on his platform. US President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Zhao and Binance have been key supporters of cryptocurrency ventures by US President Donald Trump and his family.

sources.news_title: Suspected billion-dollar Binance hack sends fear through crypto
sources.text:
Bitcoin fell as much as 3.7% – below US$79,000 and its lowest level since September – as the United States trading day was wrapping up, with other tokens also selling off. US stocks also ended the session lower, with the Nasdaq 100 tech index dropping nearly 1.4%.
“Hot wallets getting drained is not something new to crypto, but the amount would be a meaningful hack on the largest crypto exchange,” said James Seyffart at Bloomberg Intelligence. “It’s definitely a bad look. And this is one after another,” he said of a recent spate of security incidents.
Already fragile sentiment was hit further amid reports of a potential security breach involving the platform Binance, which, if verified, would add to a bruising run of crypto security incidents. Within recent months, hundreds of millions of dollars were drained from Bitget, while tampering tied to Ledger devices also led to millions of dollars in losses.
Traders had already been bracing for greater volatility in the crypto market this week, with US$11b in options set to expire on Friday (US time). This comes days ahead of next week’s US midterm elections, when Democrats could potentially retake one or both chambers of Congress and open the door to greater regulatory scrutiny for the industry.
Exchange thefts and malfeasance have been an ever-present backdrop of crypto’s almost two-decade ascent and have occasionally provoked protracted bear markets in the currency, the most famous of which was the collapse of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX in November 2022. 
In what remains perhaps the most notorious hacking incident, Japan-based Bitcoin exchange Mt. Gox was struck in 2011. Over time, the hackers made off with tokens worth billions of dollars based on the current market price. Mt. Gox eventually went bankrupt.
“It’s a huge damage to crypto because of the consistent successful hacks in the space,” said Tian Zeng, chief executive officer of crypto hedge fund Third Eye. “The fact that exploits keep happening makes it dangerous in the age of newest AI models being released every two weeks.”

sources.text:
Crypto giant Binance hit by $6.3bn hack suspected to be largest in history
- Published
Cryptocurrency giant Binance said on Thursday that $6.3bn (£4.7bn) of digital assets have been impacted by what is thought to be the biggest crypto hack on record.
The world's biggest crypto exchange said about half of those assets had been frozen but that many remained in the hands of the hackers, adding that it will "cover all losses".
The company said while initial checks suggested an engineer's laptop had been compromised, allowing an attacker to make unauthorised withdrawals, "our subsequent investigation has uncovered additional points of breach".
Two analytics firms have attributed the incident, which eclipses a record-setting $1.5bn hack on the Bybit exchange in 2025, to a North Korean hacking unit called TraderTraitor.
Cyber-security firm Check Point said the unit is also known in the industry as Lazarus Group, which has been blamed for the 2025 hack.
Check Point's chief information security officer Jayant Dave said the losses estimated by Binance made it "the largest crypto theft on record".
AI-powered investigations company TRM Labs said in a report that several elements of the Binance attack resemble earlier North Korean-linked incidents, including the Bybit hack.
The lab's global head of policy Ari Redbord told the BBC the Binance hack is a "watershed moment" that is unlike anything the industry has seen.
The attacker still holds an enormous sum of stolen assets, meaning efforts to trace and recover the funds are far from over, Redbord added.
Binance, which was founded in China in 2017, allows users to trade digital assets and is estimated to have more than 300 million registered users worldwide.
The company said in 2024 that it has more than $160bn in assets under its custody.
The exchange has been subject of regulatory scrutiny around the world.
Chainalysis, a crypto analytics firm, also said it has "high confidence" that the North Korean group are linked to the hack.
For the last few years North Korea-linked operatives have focussed on attacking cryptocurrency companies for large thefts of digital tokens.
Western security agencies have previously said stolen funds are used to finance North Korea's nuclear weapons and missile development programs.
The regime has denied any involvement in hacks in the past.
Eric Jardine, Chainalysis' Head of Research, urged every exchange to remain vigilant as the platforms are attractive targets for hackers due to the sheer value of assets.
Binance did not directly respond to BBC questions about the incident's potential links to North Korea but said: "We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice."
The incident concerns Binance.com - while much smaller crypto platform Binance.US, which provides trading services specifically for American residents - said its platform is not affected by the issue.
Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said the company's initial investigation suggested the hack started with a compromised engineer's laptop.
"That gave an attacker access to a service container, where they submitted unauthorized withdrawal transactions," he said in a statement.
"To be clear: the attacker did not simply use one engineer's permissions, and this was not a single 'one-click' action. It involved a more complex attack process. Our investigation has not attributed responsibility to any individual. So far, we have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak."
He said a detailed "post-mortem" would be shared once the investigation was complete.
In an update, the company said in a statement on X that another investigation found there had been other breach points: "We are still gathering the facts, and will share more directly as we have them."
Check Point's Dave said this attack also resembled a hack on crypto exchange platform Bitget in September in which $388m (£289m) was lost: "This implies that attackers no longer need the vault keys. They target the systems and people with authority to use them."
In a series of posts, Yi He, Binance's co-chief executive, thanked various cryptocurrency issuers for freezing the assets.
"Safety first: withdrawals are currently disabled until the environment is confirmed to be secure," she said.
Two other major crypto platforms, Tether and Circle, said they had frozen a total of about $2.4bn of assets in response to the potential Binance hack.
World Liberty Financial, a crypto company linked to US President Donald Trump and his family, said it has worked with its partners to freeze stolen funds.
Crypto exchange Coinbase said it was unaffected by the incident and was monitoring the situation.
Several crypto industry observers had flagged concerns about a potential hack on Binance hours before the exchange confirmed the security issue.
Bitcoin dropped by more than 4% following the alerts. The price of other major cryptocurrencies including Ethereum and Solana also fell sharply.

sources.news_title: Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history
sources.text:
Binance says $6.3bn stolen in biggest crypto heist in history
Blockchain intelligence firm attributes attack to North Korean state-sponsored hackers.
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has said that about $6.3bn in funds have been stolen in a “security incident” that looks to be the biggest crypto heist in history.
The world’s largest crypto exchange said on Thursday that it had suspended all deposits and withdrawals and that about $3bn in funds had been frozen following the apparent hacking.
Binance said an initial investigation suggested that a hacker had been able to make unauthorised transactions after gaining access to an engineer’s compromised laptop.
The company said it would cover all losses, adding that user funds were “safe”.
“Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly,” Binance said in a statement to Al Jazeera.
“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.”
The company added that it would share a “detailed” technical post-mortem once investigations were complete.
Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder and largest shareholder, said earlier that the exchange appeared to have been hacked.
TRM, a blockchain intelligence firm, said in a report that it assessed with “high confidence” that the attack was carried out by North Korea’s hacking unit TraderTraitor, which investigators have linked to the Lazarus Group.
Ari Redbord, TRM’s global head of policy, described the attack as “unprecedented” and a “watershed”.
“When North Korea steals at this scale, the money funds weapons proliferation and other destabilising activity. That makes this a global security issue, not just a crypto theft,” Redbord told Al Jazeera.
The price of Bitcoin, the world’s most popular cryptocurrency, fell about 5 percent following the heist, dropping below $77,000.
“Binance is one of the largest centralised exchanges, and so a blow to confidence in them risks shocking confidence to many retail investors, which could dampen prices of crypto assets,” Sean Foley, an expert in crypto markets at Macquarie University in Sydney, told Al Jazeera.
Foley said the attack highlighted the risks of centralised exchanges and could spur more traders to use decentralised alternatives.
“Any assets held at a centralised exchange are only as safe as the exchange itself, and the larger the exchange’s holdings, the larger a target it becomes,” Foley said.
The Binance hacking dwarfs the previous record for a crypto theft, set in 2025 when North Korean state-backed Lazarus Group carried out a $1.5bn heist on Bybit.
Cybercriminals stole $2.87bn in crypto assets in nearly 150 hacking incidents in 2025, according to the 2026 Crypto Crime Report produced by TRM.
Binance, founded in China by Zhao in 2017, has about $155bn in assets under management, more than any other exchange, according to CoinMarketCap.

sources.text:
Binance hacked, billions in crypto stolen
Binance may have been hacked. The popular crypto exchange announced a "potential security issue" on Thursday, freezing withdrawals after an apparent hacker drained hot wallets of several billion dollars in cryptocurrency. As of 10:25 p.m ET / 7:25 p.m. PT, Binance states that the breach has impacted approximately $6.3 billion in funds.
The official Binance X account first acknowledged the issue at 5:15 p.m. ET / 2:15 p.m. PT. This came within minutes of reports that digital finance companies Tether and Circle Group had frozen significant amounts of their respective stablecoins in response to a potential hack — specifically about $971 million in Tether and $823 million in USD Coin.
Binance subsequently stated that a total of $2.54 billion had been frozen, warning that this number would potentially grow as assets were traced. By 8:52 p.m. ET / 5:52 p.m. PT, Binance approximately $3 billion had been verified as frozen.
You May Also Like
"Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating," Binance wrote. "Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information."
    
        This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.
    
Few details about the hack were initially available. However, the ostensible hacker's wallet held $1.77 billion in Tether, $1.44 billion in Bitcoin, and $1.01 billion in Ethereum, as well as over a billion more spread across other currencies such as USD Coin, Tron, and Solana.
These assets were reportedly drained from hot wallets: cryptocurrency wallets that are connected to the internet. Compared to offline cold wallets, they are significantly more practical for conducting transactions on exchanges such as Binance. However, they are also less secure.
Binance co-founder and former CEO Changpeng Zhao has stated that it "does look like a hack," but maintained a positive outlook on the situation.
"I don't manage Binance (.com) anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered," Zhao wrote on X.
In an update at 6:33 p.m. ET / 3:33 p.m. PT., Binance stated that its team was conducting security checks, and attempted to reassure anxious users.
"Withdrawals will resume as soon as the security issue is fully resolved," it wrote. "User funds remain safe."
Binance later announced at 7:06 p.m. ET / 4:06 p.m. PT that it had suspended Binance Alpha trading, which would "resume once the security issue is resolved." Binance Alpha is a platform dedicated to highlighting early-stage crypto projects, which are not yet listed on the Binance exchange.
This freeze was extended to all transactions on Binance a little over an hour later, the exchange stating that it would "cover all losses."
"As a precaution, all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while our team conducts security checks, freezes funds, and works with law enforcement," Binance posted at 8:13 p.m. ET / 5:13 p.m. PT. "This is an industry-wide effort, and we are grateful to partners across the ecosystem who have moved quickly to help freeze affected assets."
    
        This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.
    
Over five hours after Binance first acknowledged the incident, the exchange stated it may have found the source of the breach: a compromised laptop.
"Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions," Binance posted at 10:25 p.m ET / 7:25 p.m. PT. "We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak."
It further stated that it had revoked the authorisation of the potential hacker's crypto address, and elaborated on its commitment to cover any losses.
"Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe," Binance wrote in a blog post. "We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete."
The SAFU (aka Secure Asset Fund for Users) is Binance's emergency reserve fund specifically for compensating impacted individuals in the event of severe breaches such as this. Held entirely in Bitcoin, SAFU's assets were valued at $1 billion earlier this month — a sixth of the amount impacted by Thursday's hack. Binance previously stated that it would replenish SAFU if it dropped below $800 million, "helping maintain the fund at a level intended to cover potential extreme-case scenarios."
    
        This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed.
    
Binance's operations continued to be disrupted through the night. On Friday, 12:36 a.m ET / Thursday, 9:36 p.m. PT, the exchange announced that users could now make deposits, but withdrawals remained paused while it conducted a "security revamp" of the service. Withdrawals are expected to resume within 48 hours of this update.
"The incident stems from multiple factors," wrote Binance, offering further information on the breach's origin. "Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident. A comprehensive report with the root cause will follow."

sources.news_title: Musk Warns "Everyday Is Zeroday" As Rumors Swirl On News Of A Massive, $5.7 Billion Binance Hack
sources.text:
Musk Warns “Everyday Is Zeroday” As Rumors Swirl On News Of A Massive, $5.7 Billion Binance Hack
Elon Musk fired off two cryptic words as reports of a staggering Binance breach sent crypto markets into freefall, with estimates of the damage ranging so wildly that nobody yet knows how bad it actually is.
The biggest crypto story of the day drew two words from Elon Musk. At 6:33 PM ET on October 29, 2026, Musk quote-posted The Kobeissi Letter’s report of a Binance hack and wrote: “Everyday is Zeroday”. At last check, the post had drawn 17,644 likes and 1,962 retweets.
A “zero-day” is a security flaw that attackers exploit before the software maker knows it exists. The developer has zero days to prepare a fix before the damage starts. Read alongside the Binance reports, we take the post as a warning that exchanges and their users face this kind of exposure all the time. That reading is our own. Musk offered nothing beyond the two words and has given no sign of special knowledge about the incident.
Loss Estimates Range Widely as Outlets Race to Report
Binance has called the event a “security incident,” and TechCrunch reported that the exchange paused withdrawals. Estimates of the loss vary widely, and Binance has not confirmed a total. Here is what has been reported in the past few hours:
- The Kobeissi Letter, in the post Musk quoted, said wallets on the Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH), Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) and TRON (CRYPTO:TRX) networks saw outflows of $5.7 billion. That included $1.45 billion of Bitcoin and $875 million of ETH, according to The Kobeissi Letter.
- Bitcoin Magazine reported that Binance lost $5.8 billion.
- CryptoTicker reported that $2.8 billion was stolen from a Binance hot wallet. A hot wallet stays connected to the internet so an exchange can process withdrawals quickly.
- Yahoo Finance reported that $2 billion was stolen.
- Reuters reported that Tether and Circle Internet Group (NYSE:CRCL | CRCL Price Prediction) blocked $2.38 billion after Binance reported a security incident. That figure counts the stablecoin balances the two issuers locked up. It is a separate number from the total taken.
- CNBC described a potential Binance “security issue.”
- The Wall Street Journal reported that Binance’s founder said the exchange “may be” the victim of the biggest-ever crypto theft. Bloomberg reported that founder CZ said Binance “may have been hacked.”
Tether and Circle can blocked their tokens at specific wallet addresses. Issuers use that tool to stop stolen funds from moving or being swapped into other assets. For a sense of scale, our coverage in October 2022 reported that Binance blocked trading after it spotted a potential hack worth $600M. Every estimate in circulation today is several times larger than that.
Crypto Prices Fall as Hack Fears Spread
Selling started before most of the headlines appeared. BeInCrypto reported that crypto liquidations exceeded $628 million in a single hour as hack fears hit Bitcoin. A liquidation is the forced closing of a borrowed position once losses wipe out the trader’s collateral.
Binance’s native token, BNB (CRYPTO:BNB), took the hardest hit. It fell 7.11% over 24 hours to $704.28, leaving it 48.59% below its all-time high. Bitcoin slipped 3.27% to $78,620, which puts it 37.64% below its $126,080 peak from October 6, 2025. Ether lost 4.05% and now trades at $2,263.83.
Bitcoin is now below both its 20-day moving average of $81,854.49 and its 50-day average of $81,896.19. It is still above its 200-day average of $73,070.62. The token had already lost 10.23% year to date before today’s news.
Key Unknowns to Track Before the Next Move
- Confirmed figures from Binance. Reported totals range from $2 billion (Yahoo Finance) to $5.8 billion (Bitcoin Magazine). Only an official accounting will determine the number.
- Further blocked. More blocked by stablecoin issuers or other exchanges would narrow the amount attackers can actually move.
- Customer balances. None of the reports cited here has established whether customer funds were affected. Watch for the timing of any restart of withdrawals.
- Price action. BNB is the most direct read on confidence in Binance. Bitcoin’s 200-day average is the next widely tracked level below the current price.
The story is still developing, and the figures above may change as Binance and investigators release more information.

sources.news_title: Binance probes possible $5.7 billion crypto hack, possibly the biggest in history
Binance reports 'potential security issue' as stablecoin issuers freeze millions in funds
sources.text:
LOS ANGELES (AP) — Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, said Thursday it’s investigating reports of a potential security issue as its founder said the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.” The company said late Thursday the estimated total impact was at more than $6 billion, which could be one of the most significant of such security incidents on record.
It wasn’t immediately clear the extent of the damage hackers might have been able to cause, and Binance had not explicitly confirmed that funds had been pilfered. The company said its teams are “working around the clock” to resolve the issue.
“Rest assured that user funds are completely safe,” a Binance spokesperson said in a statement.
“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” the statement continued.
The company wrote on its X account that the estimated total impact sat at around $6.3 billion. It said it has worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with roughly $3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
“Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions,” the company wrote.
“We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak,” it added.
Binance said it will share more technical details once the investigation is complete and when the facts are “fully verified.”
“Our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets,” the company wrote in a separate post earlier Thursday.
Binance also said all deposits and withdrawals are temporarily suspended while it conducts security checks, freezes funds and works with law enforcement.
Stablecoin providers Tether and Circle each said they froze funds Thursday in response to the incident.
Jeremy Allaire, co-founder and CEO of Circle, wrote on X that the company had frozen the equivalent of more than $800 million in currency associated with the incident “in coordination with law enforcement.” Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said on X that the company froze the equivalent of more than $1.5 billion in currency related to “a potential Binance exchange hack.”
The price of bitcoin dropped 3.2% Thursday evening to under $79,000.
Binance was founded in 2017 by Changpeng Zhao, who in 2023 pleaded guilty to a felony related to his failure to prevent money laundering on the platform and stepped down as CEO. President Donald Trump pardoned him in 2025.
Zhao posted on X on Thursday that “User funds are safe!” but added that the incident “does look like a hack on Binance.” He added that while he doesn’t manage Binance anymore, “as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”
Zhao was released from prison last year after being sentenced for violating the Bank Secrecy Act. He was the first person ever sentenced to prison time for violations of that law, which requires U.S. financial institutions to know who their customers are, to monitor transactions and to file reports of suspicious activity. Prosecutors said no one had ever violated the regulations to the extent Zhao did. Zhao and Binance have been key supporters of some of the Trump family’s crypto enterprises.
———
AP writers Chan Ho-him and Barbara Ortutay contributed.

Binance investigates possible hack after billions moved from crypto wallets
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance is investigating a possible security breach after billions of dollars in digital assets were moved from its wallets. The issuers of two major cryptocurrencies say they have frozen more than $2.3 billion linked to the incident.
“Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating,” Binance said in a social media post on Thursday. “User funds are completely safe.”
“Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency, and we will provide updates through official Binance channels as soon as we have verified information,” Binance added. “Users should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.”
Changpeng Zhao, Binance’s founder and former CEO, said it appeared the exchange had been hacked. He said he expected all user funds to be fully covered.
Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino said the company had frozen more than $1.567 billion in USDT related to a potential Binance hack. Circle CEO Jeremy Allaire said his company had frozen more than $800 million in USDC in coordination with law enforcement.

More than $2 billion in cryptocurrencies left Binance’s online wallets on Thursday for an address created hours earlier, Yahoo Finance reported, citing blockchain data. The outlet said the transfers included ether and USDT, and that some of the funds were subsequently moved to another address.

sources.news_title: Hackers steal $6.3 billion from crypto giant Binance
sources.text:
One of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchanges, Binance, has been hit by a cyberattack in which hackers stole a record $6.3 billion.
US analysts have said that a group linked to North Korea was behind the hack with Binance reporting it had found multiple ‘points of breach’.
Binance says it has recovered around $3 billion of affected assets so far and was working with partners to freeze the remaining funds.
“Fundamental shift in cyber resilience needed”
Intelligence platform GlobalData has said the cyberattack highlights a need for a fundamental shift in cyber resilience.
“The reported $6.3 billion cyberattack on cryptocurrency exchange Binance has raised fresh concerns about the scale and sophistication of threats targeting financial intuitions,” said Phoebe Hodgson, Banking and Payments Senior Analyst at GlobalData.
“With investigators examining the possibility of compromised employee access and state-linked involvement, the incident raises uncomfortable questions about whether traditional security approaches can keep pace with increasingly sophisticated attackers.
“Attackers are no longer focused solely on breaking into systems or stealing customer data.
“They are increasingly seeking to exploit the trust embedded within financial infrastructure, turning legitimate access and transaction processes into mechanisms for moving money.
“For financial institutions, the implications are significant. Decades of investment in cybersecurity has strengthened traditional defences, yet the growing complexity of digital banking and AI have created new vulnerabilities.”
“The greatest threat to the wealth management”
“According to GlobalData’s Wealth Management Industry Conditions Analytics 2026, the greatest threat to the wealth management industry is cybersecurity threats.
“Of the institutions surveyed 65% said this was their greatest concern, up from 56% in 2025 (478 wealth management companies across 20 markets were surveyed in Q2 2026).
“Such attitudes can be relayed into retail banking, payments and other financial industries.
“As institutions become more interconnected and dependent on automated processes, the distinction between a security breach and a major financial loss is becoming dangerously narrow.
“The real challenge is that sophisticated attackers do not necessarily need to defeat every security control.
“They only need to find one trusted pathway that allows them to operate undetected.
“Once inside, the speed of modern financial transactions can leave institutions with precious little time to intervene.
“This demands a fundamental change in thinking. Cybersecurity can no longer be judged primarily by how effectively institutions keep attackers out.
“Banks must assume that some defences will eventually fail and design their operations to prevent a single compromise from becoming a financial catastrophe.
“Ultimately, the Binance hack reinforces a critical message for financial-services leaders: the next generation of cyber resilience will be defined not by whether institutions can prevent every breach, but by whether they can stop attackers from turning that breach into irreversible financial loss.”

CoinGlass figures showed $1.49 billion in cryptocurrency derivatives liquidations within 24 hours, including $1.29 billion in bullish bets. More than 243,000 traders were affected.
Bitcoin accounted for approximately $475 million of the total, with bullish positions representing nearly 88%. These figures measure forced closures of leveraged trades, not losses in Bitcoin's total market value.
When prices fall far enough, exchanges automatically close positions that no longer have sufficient collateral. Those sales can drive prices lower and trigger another round of liquidations.
“Market recovery hinges on Binance restoring confidence in exchange security and customer funds,” Zeus Research analyst Dominick John told The Block.
The ultimate extent of the breach remains uncertain. But the effect on market positioning was immediate: traders who had expected a recovery above $80,000 were caught on the wrong side of an accelerating decline.

On the upside, regaining $80,000 would be a first sign that sellers are losing control. A sustained recovery towards $82,000 would offer stronger evidence of demand returning.
Until then, the swift reversal from above $80,000 leaves Bitcoin vulnerable to another test of lower prices.

Cryptocurrency prices fell on the news, while Binance halted withdrawals and said it would cover the losses. About half the stolen assets were quickly frozen by stablecoin issuers such as Tether, Circle and the Trump-backed World Liberty Financial.
The bulk of the heist unfolded in around 20 minutes beginning late on Thursday and bore similarities to previous large attacks blamed on North Korea, according to US blockchain analysis firms TRM Labs and Chainalysis.

North Korea routinely denies that. Its mission in Geneva and embassy in China did not immediately respond to Reuters’ requests for comment.
Binance said user funds were safe and that it was working with partners to freeze some of the affected assets, with about $3 billion located so far. It expects to resume withdrawal services in the next 48 hours.
It did not mention the status of the remaining $3.3 billion.

sources.news_title: Binance Reports $6.3bn Security Breach, Freezes $3bn in Assets
sources.text:
Binance Reports $6.3bn Security Breach, Freezes $3bn in Assets
Binance has reported a major security breach involving estimated losses of $6.3 billion, but says $3 billion in affected assets have been frozen.
The company said its initial investigation pointed to a potentially compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer as the possible source of the incident. The breach reportedly allowed an attacker to access an internal service container and initiate unauthorised withdrawals.
In a security update published on Friday, 30 October 2026, the exchange explained that its investigation was still underway and that it had not established all the details surrounding the attack.
According to Binance, the compromised device may have provided an attacker with access to a service container, creating an opportunity to submit withdrawal transactions without authorisation.
However, the company stressed that investigators had found no evidence of leaked wallet private keys, an important security detail given the scale of the reported incident.
“Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions,” the company stated.
The cryptocurrency platform added that it would publish a detailed technical post-mortem once investigators had completed their work and verified the findings.
Meanwhile, Binance said it was working with blockchain partners to identify and restrict the movement of the affected funds. So far, approximately $3 billion has been frozen on-chain as part of the recovery effort.
The exchange also assured customers that they would not suffer financial losses because of the incident. It pledged to cover the affected funds using its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company resources.
“Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe,” the statement said.
The company further promised to release an updated Proof of Reserves report after completing its security improvements and other corrective measures.
As part of its immediate response, Binance temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while carrying out additional security checks.
It also withdrew authorisation from the affected address to prevent further unauthorised activity. The exchange has contacted law enforcement agencies and blockchain intelligence partners to trace the stolen assets and identify those responsible.
Binance said its technical and security teams were working continuously to contain the incident, investigate the breach and restore normal operations safely.
“Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly,” it stated.
The company also confirmed that it was cooperating with law enforcement agencies to establish the identities of the suspected attackers.
“We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice.”
The exchange urged customers to obtain further information only through its official communication channels to avoid misleading reports and possible scams. Users experiencing difficulties or requiring clarification were also directed to its customer support team.
However, Binance did not reveal the identities of the suspected attackers or provide a specific date for restoring normal deposit and withdrawal services.
The incident has placed renewed attention on cryptocurrency exchange security, particularly the risks associated with compromised employee devices and unauthorised access to internal systems.
Although the company maintains that customer funds remain protected, the scale of the reported losses and the ongoing recovery operation make the investigation an important development for the wider digital asset industry.
Can Binance’s decision to cover all reported losses restore customer confidence following such a major security incident?

sources.news_title: Binance suffers record $6.3bn cryptocurrency hack
sources.text:
Cryptocurrency exchange Binance has suffered an unprecedented security breach involving $6.3 billion (£4.7 billion) in digital assets, in what investigators believe is the largest cryptocurrency theft ever recorded.
The attack, which unfolded on 29 October 2026, targeted wallets operated by the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, with billions of dollars transferred across multiple blockchain networks in a matter of minutes.
Blockchain intelligence firm TRM Labs has attributed the attack with high confidence to TraderTraitor, a North Korean state-linked hacking group, previously connected to major cryptocurrency thefts.
According to TRM Labs, attackers moved $6.36 billion across ten blockchains, with most of the transfers completed within around 20 minutes.
The scale of the incident significantly exceeds the $1.5 billion Bybit hack in February 2025, which had previously been considered the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
Binance has confirmed a security incident affecting approximately $6.3 billion in assets, although investigations into the precise mechanism and the final financial impact remain ongoing.
In an initial security update, Binance said the incident may have involved a compromised laptop belonging to a DevOps engineer, potentially allowing the attacker to access a service container and initiate unauthorised withdrawal transactions.
The exchange said it had found no evidence that wallet private keys were directly compromised and promised to publish a detailed technical report once its investigation is complete.
Binance temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks were carried out, revoked affected authorisations and began working with law enforcement and blockchain investigators to trace the stolen assets.
The exchange has insisted that customer funds remain safe and that any losses will be covered through its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) and company reserves.
However, the incident has raised questions about how one of the world’s largest cryptocurrency platforms could experience a breach involving such substantial sums.
$3 billion in affected digital assets has already been frozen, following coordination between Binance, blockchain networks and stablecoin issuers.
Companies including Tether and Circle have participated in efforts to prevent stolen tokens from being transferred or converted into other assets.
Despite these measures, investigators believe the attackers continue to control substantial quantities of Bitcoin and Ether.
TRM Labs estimates that more than 420,000 Ether and 18,270 Bitcoin, worth $2.4 billion, remained under attacker control during its initial investigation.
Freezing digital assets can prevent attackers from moving certain tokens, but it does not automatically guarantee that the funds will be recovered or returned to their rightful owners.
Investigators believe preparations for the attack began at least 36 hours before the theft, suggesting a coordinated operation involving advance testing and the preparation of unauthorised transactions.
TRM Labs identified activity involving pre-signed transaction authorisations and the manipulation of Ethereum wallet functionality, alongside transfers across other blockchain networks.
The findings suggest the attackers may have gained access to systems capable of authorising transactions across multiple cryptocurrency networks.
However, the precise technical cause has not yet been independently established, and Binance’s internal investigation remains ongoing.
Ari Redbord, chief policy officer at TRM Labs, described the incident as extraordinary both in scale and in the speed with which the attackers moved assets.
The firm believes the operation demonstrates the increasing sophistication of state-linked cybercriminal groups targeting cryptocurrency infrastructure.
The suspected involvement of North Korea’s TraderTraitor group adds a significant national security dimension to the investigation.
The same organisation was previously linked by US authorities to the February 2025 Bybit attack, highlighting the persistent threat posed by organised hacking operations against digital asset exchanges.
Cryptocurrency markets reacted sharply to news of the breach, with Bitcoin falling towards $77,000, approximately 5% lower over the preceding 24 hours.
Other digital assets also declined as investors reassessed security risks and the potential implications for confidence in centralised cryptocurrency exchanges.
The incident has renewed debate about the protection available to cryptocurrency customers compared with users of conventional banking services.
Although Binance has pledged to cover losses, cryptocurrency holdings generally do not benefit from the same deposit protection arrangements available to eligible bank deposits, leaving customers reliant on exchange security, financial resources and applicable legal protections.
The growing relationship between cryptocurrency markets and traditional financial institutions has also prompted concerns about whether severe disruption within the digital asset sector could have wider financial consequences.
Security researchers have emphasised the importance of stronger access controls, transaction monitoring and protection of operational infrastructure, particularly where compromised employee systems could provide access to high-value financial transactions.
The incident demonstrates that blockchain transaction transparency alone cannot prevent the rapid movement of stolen assets when attackers obtain access to trusted systems.
For investors, the Binance breach represents a major test of confidence in cryptocurrency market infrastructure, with the scale of the theft potentially intensifying regulatory scrutiny and pressure for stronger security standards.
The exchange’s ability to honour its commitment to cover losses, restore normal services and establish the precise cause of the incident will be central to rebuilding confidence.
Attention will now turn to the recovery of frozen funds, the ongoing investigation into the suspected North Korean attackers and Binance’s forthcoming technical post-mortem, as the cryptocurrency industry assesses the consequences of its largest reported security breach.

“User funds are completely safe” is the bookmaker equivalent of a football club chairman’s vote of confidence in the manager.

(No, just asking. It’s not me.)
Precisely. What’s the point of stealing something that doesn’t exist?
You wash them though a number of accounts starting with ones you secretly own and then into an account that you can use at an exchange to convert to fiat currency.
I’m currently trying to give a mere £5K to one of my kids. I’m going to have to produce a witnessed letter and some sort of biometric government digital id before he can use it towards his house deposit. How the fuck am I going to explain putting $6bn into fiat currency. Crypto exchanges won’t pay a container-load of cash, it has to stay in the black economy or go into reportable accounts where the bank must tell the IRS/HMRC. Of course if I was not a person but a foreign nation things would be different.
In our “civilised” world…. yes….
But this theft has enough links to a confirmed earlier theft that fingered the Norks…
And the Norks… welll… they do things Differently….
It’s the same money laundering problem faced by all who enjoy the proceeds of crime. All those Turkish barbers aren’t there to cut hair.
Legitimately giving your kid 5k is disproportionately hard as the legal profession are involved.
I thought the whole point of the blockchain was that it was totally public. So although you don’t know who owns any given bitcoin, you can track its progress from wallet to wallet. Thus presumably the stolen bitcoin can be seen on the public register, we just don’t know who controls them at the moment.
There are randomizers – people put their crypto into a shared account, its randomized and then paid back out. This doesn’t prevent tracking but it makes the tracking exponentially harder as there are now tons of extra nodes and branches that have to be traced down to continue the trail.
Sam Bankman-Fried gave it a good try.
You find someone who doesn’t have to worry about the police (African dictators, American Congressmen,…) and offer them half. $100m a year, say, for 30 years. They get $3bn and your silence, you get £3bn you can spend and protection from investigation.
The wonderful thing about having enough money is that if you have a problem you can afford to employ someone who knows how to solve it. Granted, you have to play in the honey badgers’ hornet hive to do this, so you’re going to have to be pretty hard and horny yourself to survive. Someone with £3bn can afford to employ someone to beat the rest of it out of you. But there are probably people who can, and I imagine they are probably the ones employing the hackers.
You sell it on bit by bit to the next generation of the ‘greater fool’ scam.
Crypto does not produce liquidity, there isn’t a single dollar in crypto that did not get there by someone buying crypto. All you can do with it is sell it to someone else buying crypto or gamble (more crypto) with it. You can’t even buy drugs with it any more.
You buy in hoping to sell to someone who is a greater fool than you.
You mean to tell me that an unknown exchange, controlled by unknown actors, dealing in a unit of exchange which has no physical existence or traceability, has suffered a breach of its digital existence?
I’m shocked, shocked, I really am . . . .
llater,
llamas
Is Binance for gays only or are there some cis investors too?
Everyone relax, its all done. Your money is already gone. No need to flail around.
What is amazing is not that these things always end up as criminal scams. What is amazing is that *there are any legitimate schemes at all.*

Closing Bell: AI trade and Binance get monstered while Coles hits the bargain bin
- ASX charges early, knocks off before the finish
- Retail rebounds, Coles gets trollied, lithium stays crook
- Binance cops a monster hack as AI stocks lose the plot
The ASX spent Friday morning absolutely charging, up more than 1% at one stage. This was awesome.
But then it remembered it was Friday and wandered off for a long lunch. The bastard.
By the close, the index was still green – up 0.18% – but most of the early surge had disappeared after five beers and two bowls of fries too many.
Consumer discretionary did most of the showing off, though, as yesterday’s battered retailers bounced. Wesfarmers (ASX:WES), JB HiFi (ASX:JBH) and Nick Scali (ASX:NCK) all got off the canvas.
Coles Group (ASX:COL) did not. Eddy wrote a bit about that over a toasted ham, gruyere and pickle sandwich and a pineapple and lime kombucha at lunch.
But to summarise, the supermarket giant fell more than 12% after first-quarter sales disappointed and it warned first-half supermarket earnings would be flat. Clean up on aisle four. Actually, all the aisles.
Meanwhile, lithium also continued its week-long impersonation of a dropped pie, with Chinese carbonate futures lower again and the local names following suit.
Oh, and Catalyst Metals (ASX:CYL) joined the carnage, down more than 20% after cutting FY27 production guidance, while Reece (ASX:REH) went completely the other way, jumping about 8% after quarterly sales rose 4.3%.
TLDR on all that? Retail bounced, Coles got trollied, lithium stayed crook and the ASX knocked off early.
Here’s what else caught our eye…
- Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals after a suspected hack that may have lifted as much as US$6 billion, with the exchange blaming a compromised DevOps laptop and saying losses will be covered. North Korea’s TraderTraitor group is now being blamed. Biggest ever crypto hack? Pfft… just a regular day at the office for crypto.
- Alphabet lost about US$500bn in market value after investors decided Google’s AI search push might be brilliant at answering questions and less brilliant at making money. Awkward.
- Microsoft went looking for about US$25bn in debt and got more than US$100 billion of orders. Must be nice having banks fight over who gets to lend you money.
- Amazon slid around 7% after hours and Intel fell more than 20%, extending the sudden outbreak of nerves around AI spending. Tell you what, the future’s having a bloody difficult Friday.
- Bitcoin fell below US$77,000 during the Binance mess, while BNB and Ethereum also copped it. “Crypto Twitter” has, of course, been completely normal and rational about all of this…
Just in: Exclusive footage of how the Binance hacker operated!!!

Movers and Shakeouts
Consumer discretionary came roaring back on Friday, up 2.73% after spending most of the week being kicked between the legs.
Industrials added 1.15%, energy rose 0.97%, healthcare gained 0.84% and telcos put on 0.79%. Eight sectors finished higher, which sounds more convincing than the ASX 200’s actual 0.18% gain.
Because underneath it, there was still plenty of mess.
Tech fell 1.34%, staples lost 0.97% and materials dropped 0.87%. The All Tech index fell 0.76%, resources lost 0.72% and the Small Ords were down 0.74%.
Gold also got punted, with the ASX All Ordinaries Gold index down 2.17%.
So yes, the market finished green. Just don’t look too closely at it all, okay?
TLDR? Retail came back from the dead, tech fell over, gold got mugged and the ASX somehow still finished in the green. Is it pub o’clock yet?

sources.news_title: Binance hit by potentially biggest crypto hack in history: $6.3 billion affected, who is behind it?
sources.text:
Binance hit by potentially biggest crypto hack in history: $6.3 billion affected, who is behind it?
Binance is investigating an alleged $6.3 billion cryptocurrency security breach, with questions emerging over how attackers gained access and how much money can be recovered. Here is what we know about the reported attack, Binance's response, suspected hackers and the biggest cryptocurrency exchange hacks in history.
The cryptocurrency industry has been hit by another major security scare, and this time the numbers are staggering. Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, is investigating a cyberattack involving an estimated $6.3 billion in digital assets. The incident came to light on October 29, with billions of dollars moving out of wallets linked to the exchange. If the full amount is confirmed as stolen, this could become the largest cryptocurrency hack ever recorded.
Binance has confirmed the security incident and says around $3 billion in affected assets have already been frozen. The company has promised to cover losses, but investigators are still trying to establish exactly what happened and how much money attackers managed to take away. Reuters and TechCrunch reported on the incident as cryptocurrency markets reacted to the news.
Binance’s initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions. We have found no evidence of any wallet private key leak. We will share a detailed technical post-mortem once the investigation is complete and the facts are fully verified.
The estimated total impact sits at around $6.3B. We have worked with blockchain partners to freeze affected assets, with ~$3 billion frozen on-chain so far.
Binance will cover all losses from the SAFU fund and the company’s funds. User funds are safe. We will also publish an updated Proof of Reserves once the remediation is complete. As an immediate precaution, Binance has: – temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals while security checks are completed;
– revoked the affected address authorisation;
– engaged law enforcement and blockchain intelligence partners to trace and recover funds. Our teams are working around the clock to resolve this issue safely and thoroughly. We are working closely with our law enforcement partners to confirm the identity of these criminals and bring them to justice. Please rely only on official Binance channels for updates. Please feel free to contact Binance Customer Support if you have any further questions. https://t.co/ywB2mKFy0p — Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026
What happened in the Binance crypto hack?
According to Binance’s preliminary investigation, hackers may have compromised a laptop belonging to one of its DevOps engineers, an employee responsible for maintaining technical systems. The attacker allegedly used that access to enter a service container and initiate unauthorised cryptocurrency withdrawals. Interestingly, Binance says investigators have found no evidence that hackers obtained the private keys used to control its cryptocurrency wallets. This raises questions about how an attacker managed to authorise such large transactions without stealing those keys. Read more: Beware of MR ROBOT malware: Fake Aadhaar and KYC apps target Indian bank users
How much cryptocurrency was allegedly stolen?
Binance estimates that the incident affected approximately $6.3 billion in cryptocurrency. Around $3 billion has been frozen, leaving roughly $3.3 billion whose recovery status remains unclear.
| Details | Reported amount | 
|---|---|
| Total estimated impact | $6.3 billion | 
| Cryptocurrency frozen | $3 billion | 
| Remaining amount not confirmed recovered | $3.3 billion | 
| Previous record, Bybit hack in 2025 | Around $1.5 billion | 
Service Update
Deposits remain unaffected and continue to operate as normal.
Withdrawals remain paused while our team completes a security revamp of the withdrawal service and its related addresses. We expect to resume within 48 hours, and will update with further details.
The incident stems from multiple factors. Our security team is tracing the full attack path through the compromised computer which may be the entry point of the incident. A comprehensive report with the root cause will follow.
We will continue to share updates through official Binance channels.
— Binance (@binance) October 30, 2026
What is Binance saying about the hack?
In its October 30 statement, Binance said, “User funds are safe.”
The exchange confirmed that it had temporarily suspended deposits and withdrawals during security checks. It has revoked the affected address authorisation and contacted law enforcement.
Binance co-founder Yi He told Reuters, “Binance will cover all hacking losses.”
The company plans to use its SAFU emergency reserve and corporate funds to compensate for losses.
Read more: Hisense smart TV privacy flaw exposed 5.7 crore viewing records: What happened?
Who is behind the Binance hack?
The attackers’ identities remain unconfirmed.
According to The Washington Post, cybersecurity firms TRM Labs and Pangolin Intelligence have linked the incident to TraderTraitor, a North Korean-backed hacking group.
The group has previously been associated with major cryptocurrency thefts, including the 2025 Bybit attack. Binance has not publicly confirmed that attribution.
Read more: China-linked Storm-0940 hackers use AI tool ARTEX to launch 2,900 login attempts per minute
What happens next?
Investigators will now focus on tracing the remaining cryptocurrency, identifying the attackers and checking whether the stolen assets can be recovered.
Binance has promised a detailed technical report and updated proof of reserves once its investigation and security repairs are complete.
Read more: Why eight compromised eMudhra certificates raised an HTTPS warning
Biggest crypto exchange hacks in history: Bybit, WazirX, Mt. Gox and more
Cryptocurrency exchanges have faced several major cyberattacks over the years, with hackers stealing billions of dollars in digital assets. One of the biggest incidents took place in February 2025, when hackers stole approximately $1.5 billion from Bybit. Investigators linked the attack to North Korea’s Lazarus Group. The hackers reportedly manipulated a transaction approval process to gain control of cryptocurrency stored in a wallet.
India has faced similar incidents. In July 2024, cryptocurrency exchange WazirX lost around $235 million after attackers compromised one of its wallets. The breach affected thousands of Indian investors and raised questions about how exchanges protect customer funds.
Other major incidents include Japan’s Coincheck hack in 2018 and the collapse of Mt. Gox following years of cryptocurrency theft.
| Crypto exchange | Year | Approximate amount stolen | 
|---|---|---|
| Bybit | 2025 | $1.5 billion | 
| Coincheck | 2018 | $530 million | 
| Mt. Gox | 2014 | $470 million | 
| DMM Bitcoin | 2024 | $305 million | 
| WazirX | 2024 | $235 million | 
| Binance | 2019 | $40 million | 
Binance itself suffered a security breach in May 2019, when hackers stole around 7,000 Bitcoin worth approximately $40 million at the time. The exchange covered the losses using its emergency funds.
If the latest alleged $6.3 billion Binance incident is independently confirmed, it would exceed the scale of these earlier attacks by a considerable margin.

sources.news_title: Binance Hot Wallets Hit by Suspected $5.6B Exploit as Tether and Circle Freeze Billions
sources.text:
[Breaking – Update] Binance Hot Wallets Hit by Suspected $5.6B Exploit as Tether and Circle Freeze Billions
Update on October 30, 2026 at 11:35 am (UTC+8):
Original article follows:
Binance is actively reviewing a potential major security breach after on-chain data revealed abnormal transfers exceeding $5.5 billion across multiple network hot wallets. In response, major stablecoin issuers have moved swiftly to freeze more than $2.3 billion in assets linked to the suspected exploit addresses.
The Incident at a Glance
- Scale of Outflows: On-chain tracking services, including Hyperdash, recorded unauthorized outflows totaling roughly $5.6 billion across Ethereum, Bitcoin, and TRON networks.
- Affected Assets: Drained holdings reportedly comprise $2.29B in USDT, $1.45B in Bitcoin (~18,270 BTC), $823M in USDC, $451M in Ether (~197,000 ETH), alongside tens of millions in secondary tokens such as TRX, RLUSD, and WBETH.
- Issuer Freezes: Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino confirmed the freezing of over $1.567 billion in USDT, with total stablecoin blacklists surpassing $2.3 billion once combined with Circle’s halt of $823 million in USDC.
- Market Impact: The sudden asset movements triggered sharp liquidations exceeding $600 million across perpetual markets, alongside temporary pullbacks in major tokens.
Official Statements and Reassurances
Binance published a direct security notice confirming that internal teams are aware of anomalous activity and are prioritizing asset safety:
“Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating. User funds are completely safe. Our security teams are reviewing all relevant information with urgency.”
Former CEO and major shareholder Changpeng “CZ” Zhao also addressed the community via X, acknowledging the nature of the breach while reiterating confidence in exchange backing:
“It does look like a hack on Binance. Appreciate the quick freeze from Tether and Circle. I don’t manage Binance (.com) anymore, but as a shareholder, I expect all user funds will be fully covered.”
Key Takeaways for Traders and Account Holders
- SAFU Reserve Precedents: Binance maintains historical reserve backstops, primarily its Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), designed to backstop hot wallet shortfalls without passing haircuts to account holders.
- Centralized Blacklists as Shock Absorbers: The rapid invocation of blacklist functions by Tether and Circle demonstrates how centralized stablecoins can significantly contain net attacker proceeds during high-value exchange incidents.
- Phishing and Impersonation Caution: Binance urged users to exercise extreme caution against copycat announcements, fraudulent claims of “wallet verification,” or unsolicited compensation links circulating during ongoing investigations. Official updates will be provided exclusively through verified exchange channels.
